title.zh: 卷224 列傳十一 张煌言 张名振 王翊等 郑成功子：锦 锦子：克塽 李定国
title.en: Volume 224 Biographies 11: Zhang Huangyan, Zhang Mingzhen, Wang Yideng, Zheng Chenggong Son: Jin, Jin Son: Ke Shuang, Li Dingguo
title.raw: 卷224 列傳十一 张煌言 张名振 王翊等 郑成功子：锦 锦子：克塽 李定国

sentences.zh: 張煌言，字玄箸，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Huangyan, style name Xuanzhu, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huangyan, whose style was Xuanzhu, came from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎十五年舉人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of the Chongzhen reign of Ming he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as a provincial graduate in the fifteenth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 時以兵事急，令兼試射，煌言三發皆中。

translations.literal: Because military affairs were urgent at the time, candidates were also tested in archery; Huangyan shot three times and hit each time.
translations.idiomatic: With war pressing, candidates were also tested in archery; Huangyan fired three arrows and hit the mark every time.

sentences.zh: 慷慨好論兵事。

translations.literal: He was ardent and fond of discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was passionate and loved to talk of military strategy.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，師定江寧，煌言與裏人錢肅樂、沈宸荃、馮元颺等合謀奉魯王以海。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, when the imperial army secured Jiangning, Huangyan joined his fellow townsman Qian Sule, Shen Chenquan, Feng Yuanyang, and others in a plot to enthrone Prince Lu, Zhu Yihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, after the Qing army took Jiangning, Huangyan plotted with his neighbors Qian Sule, Shen Chenquan, Feng Yuanyang, and others to set up Prince Lu Zhu Yihai as ruler.

sentences.zh: 煌言迎於天台，授行人。

translations.literal: Huangyan received him at Tiantai and was appointed Bearer of Dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan welcomed the prince at Tiantai and was made Bearer of Dispatches.

sentences.zh: 至紹興，稱「監國」，授翰林院修撰。

translations.literal: When they reached Shaoxing, he was styled "Regent of the State" and appointed Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaoxing the prince took the title "Regent of the State," and Huangyan was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 入典制誥，出領軍旅。

translations.literal: Within the court he oversaw edicts and proclamations; in the field he commanded the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In court he drafted state documents; in the field he led the troops.

sentences.zh: 三年，師潰。

translations.literal: In the third year the army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year their forces were shattered.

sentences.zh: 歸與父母妻子決，從王次石浦，與黃斌卿軍相犄角，加右僉都御史。

translations.literal: He returned home to bid farewell to his parents, wife, and children, followed the prince to encamp at Shipu, and with Huang Binqing's army formed a pincer position; he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to take leave of his parents, wife, and children, then followed the prince to Shipu, where his forces and Huang Binqing's held a mutual defensive line; he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 魯王諸將，張名振最強。

translations.literal: Among Prince Lu's generals, Zhang Mingzhen was the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Of Prince Lu's commanders, Zhang Mingzhen was the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 四年，江南提督吳勝兆請降，煌言勸名振援勝兆，遂監其軍以行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jiangnan Military Governor Wu Sheng Zhao asked to surrender; Huangyan urged Mingzhen to aid Sheng Zhao, and then supervised the army on the march.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Jiangnan military governor Wu Sheng Zhao offered to defect; Huangyan persuaded Mingzhen to support him and went along to oversee the expedition.

sentences.zh: 至崇明，颶作，舟覆，煌言被執。

translations.literal: When they reached Chongming a typhoon arose, the boats capsized, and Huangyan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Off Chongming a typhoon struck, the fleet overturned, and Huangyan was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 七日，有導之出者，走間道復還入海。

translations.literal: After seven days someone guided him out; he fled by a hidden path and returned to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day a guide helped him escape; he took a back trail and made his way back to sea.

sentences.zh: 經黃岩，追者圍而射之，以數騎突出，自是益習騎射。

translations.literal: Passing through Huangyan, pursuers surrounded and shot at him; he broke out with a few horsemen, and from then on practiced mounted archery all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Near Huangyan pursuers hemmed him in and shot at him; he broke through with a handful of riders and afterward trained harder in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 集義旅屯上虞、平岡。

translations.literal: He gathered righteous volunteers and encamped at Shangyu and Pinggang.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied loyalist volunteers and stationed them at Shangyu and Pinggang.

sentences.zh: 諸山寨多出劫掠，獨煌言與?王翊履畝勸輸，戢所部毋擾民。

translations.literal: Most mountain strongholds turned to plunder, but Huangyan alone, with Wang Yideng, went field by field urging payment of grain tax and restrained his men from harassing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Most rebel camps lived by raiding, but Huangyan and Wang Yideng alone walked the fields to collect taxes in grain and kept their troops from molesting civilians.

sentences.zh: 六年，覲王於健跳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he had an audience with the prince at Jiantiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he went to Jiantiao to pay court to the prince.

sentences.zh: 七年，名振奉王居舟山，召煌言入。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Mingzhen installed the prince on Zhoushan and summoned Huangyan to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Mingzhen settled the prince on Zhoushan and called Huangyan in.

sentences.zh: 乃以平岡兵授劉翼明、陳天樞，率親軍赴之，加兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He then entrusted the Pinggang troops to Liu Yiming and Chen Tianqu, led his personal guard to join them, and was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Pinggang force with Liu Yiming and Chen Tianqu, marched in with his personal guard, and was made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 八年，聞父訃，浙江提督田雄書招降，卻之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he heard of his father's death; Zhejiang Military Governor Tian Xiong wrote inviting him to surrender, and he refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year word came of his father's death; Zhejiang military governor Tian Xiong wrote urging him to surrender, and he declined.

sentences.zh: 師攻滃洲，名振奉王侵吳淞，冀相牽制。

translations.literal: The imperial army attacked Yuzhou; Mingzhen escorted the prince in a raid on Wusong, hoping to draw the enemy off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army attacked Yuzhou, Mingzhen led the prince in a strike on Wusong, hoping to tie down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 俄，師破舟山，乃奉王入金門，依鄭成功。

translations.literal: Soon the imperial army took Zhoushan; they then escorted the prince to Jinmen and relied on Zheng Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Qing took Zhoushan; they brought the prince to Jinmen and placed themselves under Zheng Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 成功用唐王隆武號，事魯王但月上豚、米，修寓公之敬。

translations.literal: Chenggong used the Longwu reign title of the Tang Prince, and toward Prince Lu he merely sent pork and rice each month, observing the courtesy due a guest prince.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong kept the Longwu era of the Tang Prince, while toward Prince Lu he sent only monthly rations of pork and rice, treating him as an honored guest in exile.

sentences.zh: 煌言嘗謂成功曰：「招討始終為唐，真純臣也！」

translations.literal: Huangyan once said to Chenggong: "The Grand Marshal has served the Tang from first to last — a truly loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan once told Chenggong, "You have stood by the Tang from beginning to end — a minister of pure loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 成功亦曰：「侍郎始終為魯，與吾豈異趨哉？」

translations.literal: Chenggong also said: "The Vice Minister has served Lu from first to last — are our aims not the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong replied, "And you have stood by Lu from beginning to end — are we not marching toward the same goal?"

sentences.zh: 故與成功所事不同，而其交能固，王亦賴以安居。

translations.literal: Thus although the lords they served differed, their friendship held firm, and the prince also relied on this to live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Though they served different princes, their bond held, and the prince too could live in security because of it.

sentences.zh: 九年，監名振軍，經舟山至崇明，進次金山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he supervised Mingzhen's army, passed through Zhoushan to Chongming, and advanced to camp at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he oversaw Mingzhen's forces, sailed via Zhoushan to Chongming, and moved up to Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 十年，復至崇明，師與戰，敗績。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they again reached Chongming; the imperial army fought them and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year they returned to Chongming; the Qing army met them in battle and they suffered a defeat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又自吳淞入江，逼鎮江，登金山，望祭明太祖陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year they again entered the Yangtze from Wusong, pressed on Zhenjiang, climbed Jinshan, and gazed toward the tomb of the Ming Founder to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they entered the Yangtze again from Wusong, threatened Zhenjiang, climbed Jinshan Hill, and offered sacrifice in sight of the tomb of the Ming founder.

sentences.zh: 烽火達江寧，俄，退次崇明。

translations.literal: Beacon fires were seen as far as Jiangning; soon they withdrew to Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm fires blazed as far as Jiangning; before long they fell back to Chongming.

sentences.zh: 再入江，略瓜洲、儀真，薄燕子磯，尋還屯臨門，皆與名振俱。

translations.literal: They entered the river again, raided Guazhou and Yizhen, pressed on Yanziji, and soon returned to encamp at Linmen — all with Mingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the river once more, harried Guazhou and Yizhen, drew near Yanziji, and soon withdrew to Linmen — always alongside Mingzhen.

sentences.zh: 十二年，成功遣其將陳六禦與名振取舟山，台州守將馬信約降，煌言以沙船五百迎之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Chenggong sent his general Chen Liuyu with Mingzhen to recover Zhoushan; Taizhou garrison commander Ma Xin agreed to surrender, and Huangyan met them with five hundred sand junks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Chenggong sent Chen Liuyu with Mingzhen to retake Zhoushan; Ma Xin, the Taizhou commander, agreed to defect, and Huangyan welcomed them with five hundred sand junks.

sentences.zh: 名振中毒卒，遺言以所部屬煌言。

translations.literal: Mingzhen died of poison; his last words placed his command under Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen died of poisoning and in his final words left his troops to Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，師再破舟山，煌言移軍秦川，王去「監國」號，通表桂王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the imperial army again took Zhoushan; Huangyan moved his army to Qinchuan, the prince dropped the title "Regent of the State," and sent memorials to the Gui Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Qing retook Zhoushan; Huangyan shifted his forces to Qinchuan, the prince abandoned the title "Regent of the State," and opened relations with the Gui Prince.

sentences.zh: 十四年，桂王使至，授煌言兵部侍郎、翰林院學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an envoy of the Gui Prince arrived and appointed Huangyan Vice Minister of War and Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Gui Prince's envoy arrived and made Huangyan Vice Minister of War and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督郎廷佐書招煌言，煌言以書報，略曰：「來書揣摩利鈍，指畫興衰，庸夫聽之，或為變色，貞士則不然。

translations.literal: Liangjiang Governor-General Lang Tingzuo wrote to win Huangyan over; Huangyan replied in a letter, in part: "Your letter weighs gain and loss and charts rise and fall; a common man who heard it might change countenance, but a steadfast man would not.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang governor-general Lang Tingzuo wrote to recruit him; Huangyan answered in part: "You weigh profit and loss and chart rise and fall; a timid man might waver at such words, but not a man of constancy.

sentences.zh: 所爭者天經地義，所圖者國恤家仇，所期待者豪傑事功。

translations.literal: What we contend for is heaven's law and earth's right; what we seek is the nation's grief and the family's vengeance; what we await is the achievement of heroes.
translations.idiomatic: We fight for righteousness itself, we strive for the nation's sorrow and our clans' blood-debt, and we look to the deeds of great men.

sentences.zh: 聖賢學問，故每氈雪自甘，膽薪深厲，而卒以成事。

translations.literal: The learning of sages and worthies is why they often gladly slept on felt in the snow and slept on brushwood to taste gall, yet in the end accomplished their task.
translations.idiomatic: The sages endured felt in the snow and slept on brushwood tasting gall — and in the end they prevailed.

sentences.zh: 僕于將略原非所長，祗以讀書知大義。

translations.literal: I am not by nature skilled in strategy; I know only the great principle from reading books.
translations.idiomatic: I have no gift for strategy; I know only the great duty books teach.

sentences.zh: 左袒一呼，甲盾山立，濟則賴君靈，不濟則全臣節。

translations.literal: At one call to bare the left arm, armor and shields rise like a mountain; if we succeed we rely on your spirit, if we fail we preserve our ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: One call to arms and armor stacks like a hill; if we win, it will be by your blessing — if we lose, we keep our loyalty intact.

sentences.zh: 憑陵風濤，縱橫鋒鏑，今逾一紀矣，豈復以浮詞曲說動其心哉？

translations.literal: Riding the wind and waves, crossing blades for more than twelve years now — how could empty words and crooked persuasion move my heart?
translations.idiomatic: For more than twelve years I have ridden the storms and crossed blades — do you think smooth talk can sway me now?

sentences.zh: 來書溫慎，故報數行。

translations.literal: Your letter was warm and careful, so I reply in a few lines.
translations.idiomatic: Your tone was courteous, so I answer briefly.

sentences.zh: 若斬使焚書，適足見吾意之不廣，亦所不為也。」

translations.literal: To behead the envoy and burn the letter would only show my mind was narrow — that too I will not do."
translations.idiomatic: To kill your messenger and burn your letter would only show me petty — and I will not do that either.

translations.literal: (closing quotation mark)
translations.idiomatic: End of quotation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，與成功會師將入江，次羊山，遇颶，引還。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he joined Chenggong to enter the Yangtze, anchored at Yangshan, met a typhoon, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he united with Chenggong for a Yangtze campaign, lay at Yangshan, was struck by a typhoon, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 十六年，成功復大舉，煌言與俱，次崇明。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Chenggong mounted another great campaign; Huangyan went with him and anchored at Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Chenggong launched another major offensive; Huangyan accompanied him and halted at Chongming.

sentences.zh: 煌言曰：「崇明，江、海門戶。

translations.literal: Huangyan said: "Chongming is the gateway between river and sea.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan said, "Chongming is the gateway between river and sea.

sentences.zh: 宜先定營於此，庶進退有所據。」

translations.literal: We should first establish a camp here so that advance and retreat have a base."
translations.idiomatic: We should secure a base here first, so advance and retreat have something to rest on."

sentences.zh: 成功不從。

translations.literal: Chenggong did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 師防江，金、焦兩山間橫鐵索，隔江置大砲，煌言以十七舟翦江而渡。

translations.literal: The imperial army defended the river; iron chains were stretched between Jin and Jiao hills, and great guns were set on the opposite bank; Huangyan crossed the river with seventeen boats in a wedge.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing lined the river with iron chains between Jin and Jiao hills and heavy guns on the far bank; Huangyan forced the crossing with seventeen boats.

sentences.zh: 成功破瓜洲，欲取鎮江，慮江寧援至，煌言曰：「舟師先搗觀音門，南京自不暇出援。」

translations.literal: Chenggong took Guazhou and wished to take Zhenjiang, fearing relief from Jiangning; Huangyan said: "Let the fleet first strike Guanyin Gate — Nanjing will have no leisure to send aid."
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong took Guazhou and aimed at Zhenjiang, fearing relief from Jiangning; Huangyan urged, "Send the fleet first against Guanyin Gate — Nanjing will be too busy to help."

sentences.zh: 成功以屬煌言，煌言所將人不及萬，舟不滿百，即率以西。

translations.literal: Chenggong entrusted this to Huangyan; Huangyan commanded fewer than ten thousand men and fewer than a hundred boats, and at once led them west.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong gave him the task; with fewer than ten thousand men and under a hundred ships Huangyan marched west at once.

sentences.zh: 降儀真，進次六合，聞成功拔鎮江，煌言致書，言當先撫定夾江郡縣，以陸師趨南京，成功復不從。

translations.literal: Yizhen surrendered; he advanced to Liuhe; hearing that Chenggong had taken Zhenjiang, Huangyan wrote urging that the counties along both banks be pacified first and land forces sent against Nanjing — Chenggong again would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen submitted; he moved on to Liuhe; when he heard Chenggong had taken Zhenjiang he wrote urging him to secure the river counties first and march on Nanjing by land — again Chenggong refused.

sentences.zh: 煌言進薄觀音門，遣別將以輕舟數十直上攻蕪湖，分兵掠江浦。

translations.literal: Huangyan pressed on Guanyin Gate, sent a subordinate with several dozen light boats straight up to attack Wuhu, and detached troops to raid Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan closed on Guanyin Gate, sent a lieutenant with dozens of light craft straight upriver against Wuhu, and detached men to raid Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 成功水師至，會蕪湖已降，趣煌言往撫，部勒諸軍，分道略地，移檄諸郡縣。

translations.literal: Chenggong's fleet arrived; Wuhu had already surrendered; he urged Huangyan to go pacify the region, array the armies, send columns to seize territory, and issue proclamations to the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong's fleet came up; Wuhu had already fallen; he pressed Huangyan to pacify the region, marshal the armies, send columns to seize ground, and proclaim his authority to every county.

sentences.zh: 於是太平、甯國、池州、徽州、廣德及諸屬縣皆請降，得府四、州三、縣二十四。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taiping, Ningguo, Chizhou, Huizhou, Guangde, and their subordinate counties all asked to surrender; he gained four prefectures, three departments, and twenty-four counties.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping, Ningguo, Chizhou, Huizhou, Guangde, and their dependencies all offered submission; he held four prefectures, three sub-prefectures, and twenty-four counties.

sentences.zh: 煌言所過，秋毫無犯，經郡縣，入謁孔子廟，坐明倫堂，進長吏，考察黜陟，略如巡按行部故事，遠近回應。

translations.literal: Where Huangyan passed not a hair was harmed; passing through prefectures and counties he entered the Confucius temple, sat in the Hall of Bright Doctrine, received the chief officials, examined them for promotion and dismissal — much like a touring censor's circuit — and near and far responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Huangyan went his men took nothing; in each county he visited the Confucius temple, sat in the Hall of Bright Doctrine, summoned the magistrates, and judged who should stay or go — much like a touring inspector — and the country answered from far and near.

sentences.zh: 方如徽州受降，聞成功敗，還蕪湖收兵，冀聯合瓜洲、鎮江軍為守計，既，聞成功並棄瓜洲、鎮江入海，煌言兵遂潰。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to go to Huizhou to accept surrender, he heard Chenggong had been defeated; he returned to Wuhu to gather troops, hoping to unite with the armies at Guazhou and Zhenjiang for defense; then he heard Chenggong had abandoned both Guazhou and Zhenjiang and gone to sea, and Huangyan's army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He was on his way to Huizhou to accept surrender when word came that Chenggong had lost; he fell back to Wuhu to rally his men, hoping to join forces with Guazhou and Zhenjiang; then he learned Chenggong had abandoned both places for the sea, and Huangyan's army broke apart.

sentences.zh: 南江總督郎廷佐發舟師斷煌言東下道，書招煌言。

translations.literal: South-of-the-River Governor-General Lang Tingzuo sent a fleet to cut Huangyan's route eastward and wrote to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tingzuo, governor-general south of the Yangtze, sent ships to block Huangyan's retreat east and wrote urging him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 煌言拒不應，率餘兵道繁昌，謀入鄱陽湖。

translations.literal: Huangyan refused to answer and led his remaining troops by way of Fanchang, planning to enter Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan ignored him and led his survivors toward Fanchang, intending to reach Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 次銅陵，師自湖廣至，煌言與戰而敗，撫殘兵僅數百，退次無為，焚舟登陸。

translations.literal: He halted at Tongling; the imperial army came from Huguang; Huangyan fought and was defeated, gathered the remnant of only several hundred, withdrew to Wuwei, burned the boats, and went ashore.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongling the Qing army came up from Huguang; Huangyan fought and lost, rallied only a few hundred survivors, fell back to Wuwei, burned his ships, and went ashore.

sentences.zh: 自銅城道霍山、英山，度東溪嶺，追騎至，從者盡散。

translations.literal: From Tongcheng he went by way of Huoshan and Yingshan, crossed Dongxi Ridge; pursuing cavalry arrived and his followers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: From Tongcheng he crossed Huoshan and Yingshan and climbed Dongxi Ridge; pursuers caught up and his companions scattered.

sentences.zh: 煌言突圍出，變服夜行，至高滸埠，有父老識之，匿於家數日，導使出間道，渡江走建德、祁門亂山間，痁作，力疾行，至休寧，得舟下嚴州。

translations.literal: Huangyan broke out of the encirclement, changed clothes and traveled by night; reaching Gaopu Ford, an elder recognized him and hid him at home for several days, then guided him out by a hidden path; he crossed the river and fled through the wild mountains of Jiande and Qimen; malaria struck but he forced himself on to Xiuning, found a boat, and went downriver to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan broke through, disguised himself, and traveled by night; at Gaopu an old man knew him, sheltered him for days, then led him out by a back trail; he crossed the Yangtze and fled through the wild hills of Jiande and Qimen; fever seized him but he pressed on to Xiuning, found a boat, and sailed down to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復山行，經東陽、義烏至天台達海，收集舊部，成功分兵益之，屯長亭鄉，築塘捍潮，辟田以贍軍。

translations.literal: Again he went overland through Dongyang and Yiwu to Tiantai and reached the sea, gathered his old followers, and Chenggong sent troops to reinforce him; he encamped at Changting township, built dikes against the tide, and opened fields to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: He went overland again through Dongyang and Yiwu to Tiantai and the coast, rallied his old troops, and Chenggong sent reinforcements; he settled at Changting, built seawalls against the tide, and opened fields to feed his men.

sentences.zh: 使桂王告敗，桂王敕慰問，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His envoy reported defeat to the Gui Prince; the Gui Prince issued an edict of consolation and promoted him to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His envoy told the Gui Prince of the defeat; the prince sent words of comfort and made him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十七年，移軍臨門。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he moved his army to Linmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he shifted his camp to Linmen.

sentences.zh: 十八年，廷議徙海上居民絕接濟，煌言無所得餉，開屯南田自給。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the court debated relocating coastal inhabitants to cut off supplies; Huangyan could obtain no rations and opened farms at Nantian to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the court moved coastal people inland to starve the loyalists of supplies; Huangyan could get no provisions and opened farms on Nantian to feed his men.

sentences.zh: 成功攻臺灣，煌言移書阻之，不聽。

translations.literal: Chenggong attacked Taiwan; Huangyan wrote to dissuade him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong attacked Taiwan, Huangyan wrote urging him to reconsider; Chenggong paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 師下雲南，取桂王。

translations.literal: The imperial army descended on Yunnan and captured the Gui Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army marched into Yunnan and took the Gui Prince.

sentences.zh: 煌言遣其客羅綸入臺灣，趣成功出兵，成功以臺灣方定，不能行；

translations.literal: Huangyan sent his client Luo Lun to Taiwan to urge Chenggong to march out; Chenggong said Taiwan was only just settled and could not act;
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan sent his adviser Luo Lun to Taiwan to press Chenggong to take the field; Chenggong replied that Taiwan was barely pacified and he could not march;

sentences.zh: 遣使入鄖陽山中，說十三家兵，使之擾湖廣，以緩雲南之師。

translations.literal: he sent envoys into the mountains of Xiangyang to persuade the Thirteen Families' troops to harass Huguang and ease the pressure on Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: instead he sent envoys into the Xiangyang hills to rouse the Thirteen Families and trouble Huguang, hoping to slow the Yunnan campaign.

sentences.zh: 十三家者，郝永忠、劉體純輩，故李自成部將，竄據茅麓山，衰疲不敢出。

translations.literal: The Thirteen Families were Hao Yongzhong, Liu Tichun, and their like — former generals of Li Zicheng — who had fled to hold Maolu Mountain, worn out and afraid to come out.
translations.idiomatic: The Thirteen Families were men like Hao Yongzhong and Liu Tichun, once Li Zicheng's generals, now holed up on Maolu Mountain, too weak and fearful to stir.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，煌言復移軍沙堤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, Huangyan again moved his army to Shadi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he shifted his forces again to Shadi.

sentences.zh: 成功自攻江寧敗還，取臺灣謀建國。

translations.literal: Chenggong himself, after failing in the attack on Jiangning, took Taiwan and planned to found a state.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong, defeated before Jiangning, seized Taiwan and planned to build a kingdom there.

sentences.zh: 魯王在金門，禮數日薄，煌言歲時供億，又慮成功疑，十年不敢入謁。

translations.literal: Prince Lu was at Jinmen; ceremonial observance grew daily thinner; Huangyan supplied him at the seasons, yet fearing Chenggong's suspicion, for ten years he dared not go in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu lived at Jinmen while courtesy toward him dwindled; Huangyan kept him supplied at the festivals, yet fearing Chenggong's mistrust he did not pay court for ten years.

sentences.zh: 及聞桂王敗亡，上啟魯王，將奉以號召。

translations.literal: When he heard the Gui Prince had perished, he memorialized Prince Lu, intending to uphold him as a rallying standard.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the Gui Prince was lost, he petitioned Prince Lu to take up the standard of resistance.

sentences.zh: 俄成功卒，煌言還軍臨門，又有議奉魯王監國者，煌言使勸錦，以李亞子錦囊三矢相勖。

translations.literal: Soon Chenggong died; Huangyan returned his army to Linmen; there was again talk of making Prince Lu regent; Huangyan sent someone to urge Jin, using the story of Li Yazi's brocade bag and three arrows as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chenggong died; Huangyan withdrew to Linmen; some again urged Prince Lu as regent; Huangyan sent an envoy to Zheng Jin, exhorting him with the tale of Li Yazi's brocade pouch and three arrows.

sentences.zh: 籠島，煌言不可?浙江總督趙廷臣復招煌言，煌言書謝之。

translations.literal: Caged on his island, Huangyan would not yield; Zhejiang Governor-General Zhao Tingchen again tried to win him over, and Huangyan wrote to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped on his island he would not submit; Zhejiang governor-general Zhao Tingchen tried again to recruit him, and Huangyan answered with a polite refusal.

sentences.zh: 煌言孤軍勢日促，或議入。

translations.literal: Huangyan's isolated army grew daily more pressed; some urged him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His lone force grew weaker by the day, and some urged him to defect.

sentences.zh: 二年，魯王殂，煌言慟曰：「孤臣棲棲海上，與部曲相依不去者，以吾主尚存也。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Lu died; Huangyan mourned and said: "This lone minister has lingered on the sea and clung to his troops without leaving because our lord still lived.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Prince Lu died; Huangyan grieved and said, "I have clung to the sea and kept my men only because our lord still lived.

sentences.zh: 今更何望？」

translations.literal: What hope is there now?"
translations.idiomatic: What is left to hope for now?"

sentences.zh: 三年，遂散遣其軍，居懸澳。

translations.literal: In the third year he then dismissed his army and lived at Xuan'ao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he disbanded his troops and withdrew to Xuan'ao.

sentences.zh: 懸澳在海中，荒瘠無人?，南汊港通舟，北倚山，人不能上，煌言結茅而處，從者綸及部曲數人，一侍者、一舟子而已。

translations.literal: Xuan'ao lies in the sea, barren and without inhabitants; the southern fork harbor admits boats, the north leans on mountains men cannot climb; Huangyan built a thatched hut to dwell in, with only Lun and a few followers, one attendant, and one boatman.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan'ao stood in open sea, bleak and uninhabited; boats could reach it by the southern channel, while steep hills to the north kept men away; Huangyan lived in a thatched hut with only Luo Lun, a few soldiers, one servant, and one boatman.

sentences.zh: 廷臣與提督張傑謀致煌言，得煌言故部曲，使為僧普陀，伺煌言，知蹤跡，夜半，引兵攀嶺入，執煌言及綸，與部曲葉金、王發，侍者湯冠玉。

translations.literal: Tingchen and Military Governor Zhang Jie plotted to seize Huangyan; they obtained one of Huangyan's old followers, made him a monk at Putuo, spied on Huangyan, learned his trail; at midnight they led troops climbing the ridge to enter, and captured Huangyan and Lun, with followers Ye Jin and Wang Fa, and attendant Tang Guanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen and military governor Zhang Jie plotted his capture; they turned a former soldier into a monk at Putuo to spy on him; at midnight troops climbed the ridge, seized Huangyan and Luo Lun, and took Ye Jin, Wang Fa, and the servant Tang Guanyu.

sentences.zh: 煌言至杭州，廷臣賓禮之。

translations.literal: When Huangyan reached Hangzhou, Tingchen received him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangzhou Tingchen treated him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 九月乙未，死於弼教坊，舉目望吳山，歎曰：「好山色！」

translations.literal: On the yiwi day of the ninth month he died at Bijiao Lane; he raised his eyes to Wu Hill and sighed: "What fine mountain colors!"
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwi day of the ninth month he was executed at Bijiao Lane; he looked toward Wu Hill and sighed, "What beautiful hills!"

sentences.zh: 賦絕命詞，坐而受刃，綸等並死。

translations.literal: He composed a death poem, sat, and received the blade; Lun and the others died with him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his last verses, sat upright, and met the sword; Luo Lun and the rest died with him.

sentences.zh: 煌言妻董、子萬祺先被執，羈管杭州，先煌言死。

translations.literal: Huangyan's wife, the Lady Dong, and his son Wanqi had been captured earlier, detained at Hangzhou, and died before Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Dong and his son Wanqi had been taken earlier, held at Hangzhou, and died before he did.

sentences.zh: 綸，字子木，丹徒諸生。

translations.literal: Luo Lun, style name Zimu, was a student of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Lun, styled Zimu, was a licentiate of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 方成功敗還，綸入謁，勸以回帆復取南都，成功不能用，乃從煌言。

translations.literal: When Chenggong returned defeated, Lun went to audience and urged him to turn his sails and retake the southern capital; Chenggong could not use this counsel, so Lun followed Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenggong's defeat Lun came to him and urged turning back to seize Nanjing again; Chenggong would not listen, and Lun threw in his lot with Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 又有山陰葉振名，字介韜，嘗謁煌言論兵事，煌言薦授翰林院修撰、兵科給事中。

translations.literal: There was also Ye Zhenming of Shanyin, style name Jietao, who once visited Huangyan to discuss military affairs; Huangyan recommended him and he was appointed Hanlin compiler and supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ye Zhenming of Shanyin, styled Jietao, who had visited Huangyan to talk of war; Huangyan recommended him for Hanlin compiler and supervising secretary of the military bureau.

sentences.zh: 既，復上策，欲擒斬成功，奪其兵，圖興復。

translations.literal: Later he again submitted a plan to seize and kill Chenggong, take his army, and plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Later he proposed capturing and killing Chenggong, seizing his army, and restoring the Ming.

sentences.zh: 煌言死，登越王嶺遙祭，為文六千五百餘言。

translations.literal: When Huangyan died, he climbed Prince Yue's Ridge to offer sacrifice from afar and composed a text of more than sixty-five hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: After Huangyan's death he climbed Prince Yue Ridge to mourn from afar and wrote an elegy of more than sixty-five hundred words.

sentences.zh: 與綸稱「張司馬二客」。

translations.literal: With Lun he was called "the two guests of Marshal Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: He and Luo Lun were known as "Marshal Zhang's two retainers."

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，高宗命錄勝朝殉節諸臣，得專諡者二十六；

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, the Gaozong ordered the recording of ministers of the former dynasty who died for their integrity; those granted individual posthumous titles numbered twenty-six;
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong the Gaozong ordered a roll of Ming loyalists who died for the cause; twenty-six received individual posthumous titles;

sentences.zh: 通諡忠烈百十三，煌言與焉；

translations.literal: those given the collective title Zhonglie numbered one hundred thirteen, Huangyan among them;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred thirteen shared the title Zhonglie, Huangyan among them;

sentences.zh: 忠節百八；

translations.literal: Zhongjie one hundred eight;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred eight received Zhongjie;

sentences.zh: 烈湣五百七十六；

translations.literal: Liemin five hundred seventy-six;
translations.idiomatic: five hundred seventy-six received Liemin;

sentences.zh: 節湣八百四十三。

translations.literal: Jiemin eight hundred forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: and eight hundred forty-three received Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 祀忠義祠：職官四百九十五，士民千七百二十八。

translations.literal: They were enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness: four hundred ninety-five officials and one thousand seven hundred twenty-eight commoners.
translations.idiomatic: They were honored in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness: four hundred ninety-five officials and one thousand seven hundred twenty-eight civilians.

sentences.zh: 諸與煌言並起者，錢肅樂、沈宸荃、馮元颺，明史並有傅。

translations.literal: Those who rose with Huangyan — Qian Sule, Shen Chenquan, and Feng Yuanyang — all have biographies in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Sule, Shen Chenquan, and Feng Yuanyang, who rose with Huangyan, each have biographies in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 張名振，字侯服，應天江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingzhen, style name Houfu, was a native of Jiangning in Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen, styled Houfu, came from Jiangning in Yingtian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，為石浦遊擊。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen he was patrol commander at Shipu.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Chongzhen he served as patrol commander at Shipu.

sentences.zh: 魯王次長垣，率舟師赴之，封定西侯。

translations.literal: When Prince Lu encamped at Changyuan, he led his fleet to join him and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lu made Changyuan his base, Mingzhen sailed to join him and was made Marquis of Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 以所部屯舟山，移南田，迎王居健跳所，與阮進、王朝先共擊黃斌卿。

translations.literal: He stationed his troops on Zhoushan, moved to Nantian, welcomed the prince to dwell at Jiantiao, and with Ruan Jin and Wang Chaoxian jointly attacked Huang Binqing.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Zhoushan, shifted to Nantian, brought the prince to Jiantiao, and with Ruan Jin and Wang Chaoxian attacked Huang Binqing.

sentences.zh: 斌卿，莆田人，崇禎末為舟山參將，唐王時封伯。

translations.literal: Binqing, a native of Putian, was garrison commander of Zhoushan at the end of Chongzhen and was enfeoffed as a marquis under the Tang Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Binqing of Putian was Zhoushan's garrison commander in late Chongzhen and was made a marquis under the Tang Prince.

sentences.zh: 名振奉魯王如舟山，不納。

translations.literal: Mingzhen escorted Prince Lu to Zhoushan, but Binqing would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen brought Prince Lu to Zhoushan, but Binqing refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 既，以王命進侯。

translations.literal: Later, by the prince's order, he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the prince's authority, Binqing was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 斌卿法嚴急，配民為兵，籍大戶田為官田，先後戕荊本澈、賀君堯。

translations.literal: Binqing's laws were harsh and severe; he conscripted the people as soldiers, registered great households' land as state land, and successively killed Jing Benche and He Junyao.
translations.idiomatic: Binqing ruled with harsh severity, pressed civilians into service, seized great estates for the state, and killed Jing Benche and He Junyao in turn.

sentences.zh: 王次健跳，令進告糴，又不應。

translations.literal: When the prince was at Jiantiao, Ruan Jin was sent to request grain, and again he would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was at Jiantiao, Ruan Jin was sent to buy grain, and again Binqing refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，名振破舟山，沈斌卿於海，迎王居焉。

translations.literal: At this point Mingzhen took Zhoushan, drowned Binqing at sea, and welcomed the prince to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mingzhen seized Zhoushan, drowned Binqing at sea, and installed the prince on the island.

sentences.zh: 使日本乞師，不應。

translations.literal: He sent to Japan to beg for troops; they did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Japan for military aid; they declined.

sentences.zh: 成功襲破鄭彩，名振因聲彩殺熊汝霖、鄭遵謙罪，擊破其餘兵。

translations.literal: Chenggong raided and defeated Zheng Cai; Mingzhen, citing Cai's crime in killing Xiong Rulin and Zheng Zunqian, attacked and broke his remaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong routed Zheng Cai; Mingzhen used the murders of Xiong Rulin and Zheng Zunqian as grounds to smash Cai's remaining forces.

sentences.zh: 俄，又襲殺朝先。

translations.literal: Soon after he also raided and killed Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he ambushed and killed Wang Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 師攻舟山，名振與煌言奉王南依成功。

translations.literal: The imperial army attacked Zhoushan; Mingzhen and Huangyan escorted the prince south to rely on Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing attacked Zhoushan, Mingzhen and Huangyan brought the prince south to Zheng Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 成功居王金門，名振屯?頭。

translations.literal: Chenggong lodged Prince Lu at Jinmen; Mingzhen encamped at Aotou.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong housed Prince Lu on Jinmen while Mingzhen camped at Aotou.

sentences.zh: 成功初見名振不為禮，名振袒背示之，?「赤心報國」四字，深入膚，乃與二萬人，共謀復南京，攻崇明，破鎮江，題詩金山而還。

translations.literal: When Chenggong first met Mingzhen he showed him no courtesy; Mingzhen bared his back and showed him the four characters "Loyal Heart Serving the State," tattooed deep into the flesh; then with twenty thousand men they jointly plotted to recover Nanjing, attacked Chongming, took Zhenjiang, inscribed a poem on Jinshan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong at first treated Mingzhen coldly; Mingzhen stripped to show four characters tattooed deep on his back — "A loyal heart for the state" — and with twenty thousand men they planned to retake Nanjing, struck Chongming, took Zhenjiang, left a poem on Jinshan Hill, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復與成功偕出，師次羊山，颶作，舟多損，惟名振部獨完。

translations.literal: Again he went out with Chenggong; the army anchored at Yangshan; a typhoon arose and many boats were damaged — only Mingzhen's division remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed out again with Chenggong; at Yangshan a typhoon wrecked most of the fleet — only Mingzhen's division escaped whole.

sentences.zh: 再攻崇明，復入鎮江，觀兵儀真，侵吳淞，戰屢勝。

translations.literal: He again attacked Chongming, re-entered Zhenjiang, reviewed troops at Yizhen, raided Wusong, and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Chongming again, re-entered Zhenjiang, paraded before Yizhen, harried Wusong, and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年十二月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year of Shunzhi he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Shunzhi twelve he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 或云成功酖之。

translations.literal: Some say Chenggong poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Chenggong had poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 王翊，字完勳，浙江餘姚人。

translations.literal: Wang Yideng, style name Wanjun, was a native of Yuyao in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yideng, styled Wanjun, came from Yuyao in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，起兵下管，奉魯王破上虞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi he raised troops at Xiaguan, upheld Prince Lu, and took Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi four he raised forces at Xiaguan, upheld Prince Lu, and captured Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 是時蕭山、會稽、台州、奉化民兵並起結山寨，無所得餉，則不免剽掠。

translations.literal: At this time militia in Xiaoshan, Kuaiji, Taizhou, and Fenghua all rose and formed mountain strongholds; without rations they could not avoid plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Militia across Xiaoshan, Kuaiji, Taizhou, and Fenghua rose in mountain camps; without pay they turned to raiding.

sentences.zh: 翊與煌言皆履畝科稅贍兵。

translations.literal: Yideng and Huangyan both went field by field levying tax to feed their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yideng and Huangyan both collected grain taxes field by field to pay their soldiers.

sentences.zh: 陳天樞者，會稽山寨將也，薦劉翼明佐翊，武勇善戰。

translations.literal: Chen Tianqu was a Kuaiji mountain stronghold commander; he recommended Liu Yiming to assist Yideng — brave in battle and skilled in fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tianqu, a Kuaiji hill chief, recommended Liu Yiming to aid Yideng — a fierce and capable fighter.

sentences.zh: 東徇奉化，師與遇，引卻。

translations.literal: He marched east against Fenghua; the imperial army met him and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed east into Fenghua; the Qing met him and he pulled back.

sentences.zh: 魯王授翊官，累進至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Prince Lu granted Yideng office, promoting him step by step to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu gave him rank after rank until he reached Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 復陷新昌，越餘姚，拔滸山。

translations.literal: He again took Xinchang, crossed Yuyao, and captured Hushan.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Xinchang, crossed into Yuyao, and seized Hushan.

sentences.zh: 固山額真金礪、浙江提督田雄合兵攻大嵐山。

translations.literal: Gushan Ejin Jin Jin and Zhejiang Military Governor Tian Xiong combined forces to attack Dalang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Jin, Prince of Gushan, and Zhejiang military governor Tian Xiong joined forces against Dalang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，翊走還山，團練執以獻，死定海。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year Yideng fled back to the mountains; local militia seized and handed him over, and he died at Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year Yideng fled into the hills; local militia captured him and he was executed at Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 天樞與翼明攻陷新昌，視火藥驟焚，急投水，月餘死。

translations.literal: Tianqu and Yiming attacked and took Xinchang; while inspecting gunpowder it suddenly ignited; he threw himself into the water in haste and died more than a month later.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqu and Yiming took Xinchang; gunpowder exploded as they inspected it; Tianqu leaped into the water and died a month later.

sentences.zh: 翼明善大刀，治兵戒毋犯民，翊敗，死於家。

translations.literal: Yiming was skilled with the long saber, disciplined his troops with orders not to harm the people; when Yideng was defeated, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Yiming excelled with the long saber and forbade his men to molest civilians; when Yideng fell, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 肅樂、宸荃諡忠節，翊諡烈湣，斌卿諡節湣。

translations.literal: Sule and Chenquan were posthumously titled Zhongjie; Yideng Liemin; Binqing Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Sule and Chenquan received the posthumous title Zhongjie; Yideng Liemin; Binqing Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 名振不與，而其弟名揚死舟山，諡烈湣。

translations.literal: Mingzhen was not included, but his younger brother Mingyang died at Zhoushan and was posthumously titled Liemin.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen was omitted, but his brother Mingyang, who died at Zhoushan, received Liemin.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功，初名森，字大木，福建南安人。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong, original name Sen, style name Damu, was a native of Nan'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong, born Sen and styled Damu, came from Nan'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父芝龍，明季入海，從顏思齊為盜，思齊死。

translations.literal: His father Zhilong, in the late Ming went to sea and followed Yan Siqi as a pirate; when Siqi died,
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhilong took to the sea in the late Ming and followed the pirate Yan Siqi; after Siqi's death

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，因巡撫熊文燦請降，授遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: at the beginning of Chongzhen, on the request of Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan he surrendered and was appointed Mobile Corps General.
translations.idiomatic: in early Chongzhen he surrendered at Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan's invitation and was made a mobile corps general.

sentences.zh: 以捕海盜劉香、李魁奇，攻紅毛功?，代領其，累擢總兵。

translations.literal: For capturing the pirates Liu Xiang and Li Kuiqi, attacking the Dutch at Taiwan, and taking over their command, he was repeatedly promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: For destroying the pirates Liu Xiang and Li Kuiqi, driving the Dutch from Taiwan, and taking over their bases, he rose step by step to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 芝龍有弟三：芝虎、鴻逵、芝豹。

translations.literal: Zhilong had three younger brothers: Zhihu, Hongkui, and Zhibao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong had three brothers: Zhihu, Hongkui, and Zhibao.

sentences.zh: 芝虎與劉香搏戰死。

translations.literal: Zhihu died fighting Liu Xiang in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihu was killed fighting Liu Xiang hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 鴻逵初以武舉從軍，用芝龍功舉甲科進三秩，授都指揮使。

translations.literal: Hongkui at first entered the army as a military licentiate; through Zhilong's merit he was advanced three ranks in the top tier of the military examination and appointed Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Hongkui first entered service as a military graduate; on his brother's merit he won top honors in the military exams, advanced three ranks, and became commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 累?掌印千戶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to seal-bearing chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to seal-bearing chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年，成武進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen he became a military jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen fourteen he took the military jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 明制，勳?，授錦衣遷亦至總兵。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, meritorious subjects were granted the Brocade Guard, and Qian also rose to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming custom, men of merit entered the Brocade Guard; Qian too reached regional commander.

sentences.zh: 福王立南京，皆封伯，命鴻逵守瓜洲。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established Nanjing, all were enfeoffed as marquises and Hongkui was ordered to guard Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu set up court at Nanjing, they were all made marquises and Hongkui was posted to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，師下江南，鴻逵兵敗，奉唐王聿鍵入福建，與芝龍共擁立之，皆進侯，封芝豹伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi the imperial army descended on Jiangnan; Hongkui's army was defeated; he escorted the Tang Prince Zhu Yujian into Fujian and with Zhilong jointly enthroned him; all were advanced to marquis, and Zhibao was enfeoffed as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi two the Qing swept Jiangnan; Hongkui was beaten; he brought the Tang Prince Zhu Yujian into Fujian and with Zhilong set him up as ruler; all were promoted to marquis, and Zhibao was made a marquis.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又進芝龍平國公、鴻逵定國公。

translations.literal: Before long Zhilong was further advanced to Duke of Pingguo and Hongkui to Duke of Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhilong was made Duke of Pingguo and Hongkui Duke of Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 芝龍嘗娶日本婦，是生森，入南安學為諸生。

translations.literal: Zhilong had once married a Japanese woman, who bore Sen; he entered the school at Nan'an as a student.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong had married a Japanese woman who bore Sen; the boy studied at Nan'an as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 芝龍引謁唐王，唐王寵異之，賜姓硃，為更名。

translations.literal: Zhilong presented him for audience with the Tang Prince; the Tang Prince favored him exceptionally, bestowed the imperial surname Zhu, and gave him a new name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong presented him to the Tang Prince, who favored him greatly, granted the imperial Zhu surname, and gave him a new name.

sentences.zh: 尋封忠孝伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Earl of Zhongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Earl of Zhongxiao.

sentences.zh: 唐王倚芝龍兄弟擁重兵。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince relied on the Zhilong brothers, who held great armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince relied on the Zhilong brothers and their great armies.

sentences.zh: 芝龍族人彩亦封伯，築壇拜彩、鴻逵為將，分道出師，遷延不即行。

translations.literal: Zhilong's clansman Cai was also enfeoffed as a marquis; an altar was built to appoint Cai and Hongkui as generals to march by separate routes, but they delayed and did not set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong's kinsman Cai was also made a marquis; they built an altar to commission Cai and Hongkui, but the columns delayed and did not march.

sentences.zh: 招撫大學士洪承疇與芝龍同縣，通書問，?鄉里，芝龍挾二心。

translations.literal: Pacification Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou was from the same county as Zhilong; they exchanged letters and treated each other as fellow townsmen; Zhilong harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, charged with pacification, was Zhilong's townsman; they exchanged letters as old neighbors, and Zhilong wavered in his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 三年，貝勒博洛師自浙江下福建，芝龍撤仙霞關守兵不為備，唐王坐是敗。

translations.literal: In the third year Prince Bolo's army came down on Fujian from Zhejiang; Zhilong withdrew the garrison at Xianxia Pass and made no preparations, and the Tang Prince was defeated on that account.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Prince Bolo invaded Fujian from Zhejiang; Zhilong pulled the Xianxia garrison and made no defense, and the Tang Prince was ruined.

sentences.zh: 博洛師次泉州，書招芝龍，芝龍率所部降，成功諫不聽。

translations.literal: Bolo's army halted at Quanzhou and wrote to win Zhilong over; Zhilong led his command in surrender; Chenggong remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Bolo halted at Quanzhou and summoned Zhilong; Zhilong surrendered with his troops; Chenggong pleaded in vain.

sentences.zh: 芝龍欲以成功見博洛，鴻逵陰縱之入海。

translations.literal: Zhilong wished to present Chenggong to Bolo; Hongkui secretly let him escape to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong wanted to deliver Chenggong to Bolo; Hongkui secretly let him flee to sea.

sentences.zh: 四年，博洛師還，以芝龍歸京師，隸漢軍正黃旗，授三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Bolo's army returned and took Zhilong to the capital; he was enrolled in the Plain Yellow Banner of the Chinese Eight Banners and granted a third-rank jingqi niha.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Bolo withdrew and sent Zhilong to Beijing; he entered the Plain Yellow Banner of the Chinese Eight Banners as a third-rank jingqi niha.

sentences.zh: 成功謀舉兵，兵寡，如南澳募兵，得數千人。

translations.literal: Chenggong planned to raise an army; his force was small; he went to Nan'ao to recruit and obtained several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong planned to rise in arms; his force was small, so he recruited at Nan'ao and raised several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 會將吏盟，仍用唐王隆武號，自稱「招討大將軍」。

translations.literal: He met with generals and officials in alliance, still used the Longwu reign title of the Tang Prince, and styled himself "Grand Marshal for Punitive Campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: He swore his officers to the cause, kept the Tang Prince's Longwu era name, and called himself Grand Marshal for Punitive Campaigns.

sentences.zh: 以洪政、陳輝、楊才、張正、余寬、郭新分將所部兵，移軍鼓浪嶼。

translations.literal: He assigned Hong Zheng, Chen Hui, Yang Cai, Zhang Zheng, Yu Kuan, and Guo Xin to command divisions of his troops and moved his army to Gulangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He put Hong Zheng, Chen Hui, Yang Cai, Zhang Zheng, Yu Kuan, and Guo Xin in command of his divisions and shifted to Gulangyu.

sentences.zh: 成功年少，有文武略，拔出諸父兄中，近遠皆屬目，而彩奉魯王以海自中左所改次長垣，進建國公，屯?門。

translations.literal: Chenggong was young, possessed civil and military talent, and stood out among his uncles and elder brothers; near and far all looked to him, while Cai upheld Prince Lu Zhu Yihai, moved from Zhongzuosuo to encamp at Changyuan, was advanced to Duke of Jianguo, and garrisoned Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Young Chenggong had talent in civil and military affairs and outshone his uncles and brothers; all eyes turned to him, while Cai upheld Prince Lu, moved from Zhongzuosuo to Changyuan, was made Duke of Jianguo, and held Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 彩弟聯，魯王封為侯，據浯嶼，相與為犄角。

translations.literal: Cai's younger brother Lian was enfeoffed as a marquis by Prince Lu, held Wuyu Island, and they formed a mutual defensive angle.
translations.idiomatic: Cai's brother Lian, made a marquis by Prince Lu, held Wuyu Island, and the two held a mutual line.

sentences.zh: 成功與彩合兵攻海澄，師赴援，洪政戰死。

translations.literal: Chenggong and Cai combined forces to attack Haicheng; the imperial army came to relieve it and Hong Zheng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong and Cai jointly attacked Haicheng; the Qing relieved it and Hong Zheng was killed.

sentences.zh: 成功又與鴻逵合兵圍泉州，師赴援，圍解。

translations.literal: Chenggong again joined Hongkui to besiege Quanzhou; the imperial army came to relieve it and the siege was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong and Hongkui besieged Quanzhou; Qing relief broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 鴻逵入揭陽，成功頒明年隆武四年大統曆。

translations.literal: Hongkui entered Jieyang; Chenggong issued the imperial calendar for the coming year as Longwu four.
translations.idiomatic: Hongkui entered Jieyang while Chenggong proclaimed the calendar for Longwu four.

sentences.zh: 五年，成功陷同安，進犯泉州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Chenggong took Tong'an and advanced against Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took Tong'an and pressed Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 總督陳錦師至，克同安，成功引兵退。

translations.literal: Governor-General Chen Jin's army arrived, recovered Tong'an, and Chenggong withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Chen Jin retook Tong'an and Chenggong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六年，成功遣其將施琅等陷漳浦，下雲霄鎮，進次詔安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Chenggong sent his generals Shi Lang and others to take Zhangpu, descend on Yunxiao garrison, and advance to camp at Zhao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he sent Shi Lang and others to seize Zhangpu, take Yunxiao, and advance to Zhao'an.

sentences.zh: 明桂王稱帝，號肇慶，至是已三年。

translations.literal: The Ming Gui Prince had declared himself emperor with the reign title Zhaoqing; by this time three years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: The Gui Prince had declared himself emperor under the Zhaoqing era; three years had passed since then.

sentences.zh: 成功遣所署光祿卿陳士京朝桂王，始改用永曆號，桂王使封成功延平公。

translations.literal: Chenggong sent his appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Chen Shijing to court the Gui Prince; he then first adopted the Yongli reign title; the Gui Prince's envoy enfeoffed Chenggong as Duke of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong sent Chen Shijing, his director of the imperial clan, to the Gui Prince's court, adopted the Yongli era, and was made Duke of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 魯王次舟山，彩與魯王貳，殺魯王大學士熊汝霖及其將鄭遵謙。

translations.literal: Prince Lu was at Zhoushan; Cai turned against Prince Lu and killed the prince's Grand Secretary Xiong Rulin and his general Zheng Zunqian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu was on Zhoushan when Cai turned against him and killed Grand Secretary Xiong Rulin and General Zheng Zunqian.

sentences.zh: 七年，成功攻潮州，總兵王邦俊禦戰，成功敗走。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Chenggong attacked Chaozhou; Regional Commander Wang Bangjun met him in battle and Chenggong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he attacked Chaozhou; regional commander Wang Bangjun beat him off.

sentences.zh: 攻碣石寨，不克，施琅出降。

translations.literal: He attacked Jieshi stockade but could not take it; Shi Lang went out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to take Jieshi stockade, and Shi Lang defected.

sentences.zh: 成功襲?門，擊殺聯，奪其軍，彩出駐沙埕。

translations.literal: Chenggong raided Xiamen, attacked and killed Lian, seized his army; Cai went out to garrison Shacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong struck Xiamen, killed Lian, and took his army; Cai withdrew to Shacheng.

sentences.zh: 魯王將張名振討殺汝霖、遵謙罪，擊彩，彩引餘兵走南海，居數年，成功招之還，居?門。

translations.literal: Prince Lu's general Zhang Mingzhen prosecuted Cai for killing Rulin and Zunqian and attacked him; Cai led his remnant troops to flee to the South Sea; after several years Chenggong summoned him back to dwell at Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu's general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Cai for the murders of Rulin and Zunqian; Cai fled south with his survivors; years later Chenggong recalled him to Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: Cai died.

sentences.zh: 八年，桂王詔成功援廣州，引師南次平海，使其族叔芝筦守?門。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Gui Prince ordered Chenggong to relieve Guangzhou; he led his army south to camp at Pinghai and left his clansman uncle Zhiqian to guard Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Gui Prince ordered him to relieve Guangzhou; he marched south to Pinghai and left his uncle Zhiqian to hold Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫張學聖遣泉州總兵馬得功乘虛入焉，盡攫其家貲以去。

translations.literal: Fujian Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuesheng sent Quanzhou Regional Commander Ma Degong to enter when the defense was weak and carried off all the family wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian grand coordinator Zhang Xuesheng sent Ma Degong of Quanzhou to strike while Xiamen was undefended and stripped the Zheng household bare.

sentences.zh: 成功還，斬芝筦，引兵入漳州。

translations.literal: Chenggong returned, executed Zhiqian, and led his army into Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong came back, executed Zhiqian, and marched into Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 提督楊名高赴援，戰於小盈嶺，名高敗績，進陷漳浦。

translations.literal: Military Governor Yang Minggao came to relieve; they fought at Xiaoying Ridge; Minggao was defeated and Chenggong advanced to take Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Military governor Yang Minggao came to relieve Zhangzhou; at Xiaoying Ridge he was beaten and Chenggong took Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 總督陳錦克舟山，名振進奉魯王南奔，成功使迎居金門。

translations.literal: Governor-General Chen Jin took Zhoushan; Mingzhen advanced escorting Prince Lu in flight south; Chenggong sent to welcome him to dwell at Jinmen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Chen Jin took Zhoushan; Mingzhen fled south with Prince Lu; Chenggong brought the prince to Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 九年，陷海澄，錦赴援，戰于江東橋，錦敗績。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he took Haicheng; Jin came to relieve; they fought at Jiangdong Bridge and Jin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he took Haicheng; Chen Jin relieved it but was beaten at Jiangdong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 左次泉州，成功復取詔安、南靖、平和，遂圍漳州。

translations.literal: He withdrew to camp at Quanzhou; Chenggong again took Zhao'an, Nanjing, and Pinghe, and then besieged Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell back on Quanzhou; Chenggong retook Zhao'an, Nanjing, and Pinghe and besieged Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦師次鳳凰山，為其奴所殺，以其首奔成功。

translations.literal: Jin's army halted at Fenghuang Mountain; he was killed by his slave, who took his head and fled to Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin camped at Fenghuang Mountain; a slave killed him and brought his head to Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 漳州圍八閱月，固山額真金礪等自浙江來援，與名高兵合，自長泰間道至漳州，擊破成功。

translations.literal: The siege of Zhangzhou lasted eight months; Gushan Ejin Jin Jin and others came from Zhejiang to relieve, joined Minggao's troops, reached Zhangzhou by a path through Changtai, and defeated Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Zhangzhou lasted eight months; Jin Jin came from Zhejiang, joined Minggao, slipped through Changtai, and broke Chenggong's army.

sentences.zh: 成功入海澄城守，金礪等師薄城，成功將王秀奇、郝文興督兵力禦，不能克。

translations.literal: Chenggong entered Haicheng to hold it; Jin Jin and others pressed the city; Chenggong's generals Wang Xiuqi and Hao Wenxing directed the troops in strenuous defense, and they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong withdrew into Haicheng; Jin Jin pressed the walls; Wang Xiuqi and Hao Wenxing held firm and the Qing could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 上命芝龍書諭成功及鴻逵降，許赦罪授官，成功陽諾，詔金礪等率師還浙江。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhilong to write urging Chenggong and Hongkui to surrender, promising pardon and office; Chenggong pretended assent, and an edict ordered Jin Jin and others to lead the army back to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhilong write urging Chenggong and Hongkui to surrender with pardon and rank; Chenggong feigned agreement, and Jin Jin was ordered back to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十年，封芝龍同安侯，而使齎敕封成功海澄公、鴻逵奉化伯，授芝豹左都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zhilong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tong'an, and an envoy was sent bearing an edict to enfeoff Chenggong as Duke of Haicheng and Hongkui as Earl of Fenghua, and Zhibao was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zhilong was made Marquis of Tong'an; an envoy brought edicts making Chenggong Duke of Haicheng and Hongkui Earl of Fenghua, and Zhibao was made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 芝龍慮成功不受命，別為書使鴻逵諭意，使至，成功不受命，為書報芝龍。

translations.literal: Zhilong feared Chenggong would not accept the command and wrote separately sending Hongkui to explain his intent; when the envoy arrived, Chenggong did not accept the command and wrote in reply to Zhilong.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Chenggong would refuse, Zhilong wrote separately through Hongkui; when the envoy came, Chenggong declined and answered his father in writing.

sentences.zh: 芝豹奉其母詣京師。

translations.literal: Zhibao escorted his mother to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibao brought their mother to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 成功復出掠福建興化諸屬縣。

translations.literal: Chenggong again went out raiding the subordinate counties of Xinghua in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong again raided the counties of Xinghua in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上再遣使諭成功，授靖海將軍，命率所部分屯漳、潮、惠、泉四府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor again sent envoys to instruct Chenggong, appointed him Pacification General of the Sea, and ordered him to station portions of his command in the four prefectures of Zhang, Chao, Hui, and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the court again sent envoys, made him Pacification General of the Sea, and ordered garrisons in Zhangzhou, Chaozhou, Huizhou, and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 成功初無意受撫，乃改中左所為思明州，設六官理事，分所部為七十二鎮；

translations.literal: Chenggong at first had no intention of accepting pacification; he changed Zhongzuosuo to Siming Prefecture, established six ministries to govern affairs, and divided his command into seventy-two garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong never meant to submit; he made Zhongzuosuo into Siming prefecture, set up six ministries, and divided his force into seventy-two garrisons;

sentences.zh: 遙奉桂王，承制封拜，月上魯王豚、米，並厚廩瀘、溪、甯、靖諸王，禮待諸遺臣王忠孝、沈佺期、郭貞一、盧若騰、華若薦、徐孚遠等，置儲賢館以養士。

translations.literal: he acknowledged the Gui Prince from afar, assumed authority to enfeoff and appoint, sent Prince Lu pork and rice each month, generously supported the princes of Lu, Xi, Ning, and Jing, treated with courtesy the remnant ministers Wang Zhongxiao, Shen Quanqi, Guo Zhenyi, Lu Ruoteng, Hua Ruojian, Xu Fuyuan, and others, and established the Hall for Cherishing Worthies to support scholars.
translations.idiomatic: he acknowledged the Gui Prince from afar, enfeoffed and appointed at will, sent Prince Lu monthly rations, supported the Lu, Xi, Ning, and Jing princes, honored remnant ministers such as Wang Zhongxiao, Shen Quanqi, Guo Zhenyi, Lu Ruoteng, Hua Ruojian, and Xu Fuyuan, and founded the Hall for Cherishing Worthies to sustain scholars.

sentences.zh: 名振進率所部攻崇明，謀深入，成功嫉之，以方有和議，召使還。

translations.literal: Mingzhen advanced leading his command to attack Chongming, planning a deep thrust; Chenggong was jealous of him and, because peace talks were underway, summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen led an attack on Chongming with plans to push inland; Chenggong, jealous and citing the peace talks, recalled him.

sentences.zh: 名振俄遇毒死。

translations.literal: Soon Mingzhen died by poison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Mingzhen died of poison.

sentences.zh: 成功讬科餉，四出劫掠，蔓及上游。

translations.literal: Chenggong levied grain tax as pretext and raided in all directions, spreading even to the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong taxed the countryside and raided in every direction, even reaching the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫佟國器疏聞，上密敕為備。

translations.literal: Fujian Grand Coordinator Tong Guoqi memorialized the court; the emperor issued a secret edict to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian grand coordinator Tong Guoqi reported to the throne; the emperor secretly ordered defenses prepared.

sentences.zh: 李定國攻廣東急，使成功趣會師。

translations.literal: Li Dingguo pressed the attack on Guangdong urgently and sent word for Chenggong to hurry and join forces.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo pressed hard in Guangdong and urged Chenggong to hurry and join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 成功遣其將林察、周瑞率師赴之，遷延不即進。

translations.literal: Chenggong sent his generals Lin Cha and Zhou Rui to lead troops there, but they delayed and did not advance promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong sent Lin Cha and Zhou Rui with troops to help, but they lingered and would not move.

sentences.zh: 定國敗走，成功又攻漳州，千總劉國軒以城獻，再進，復陷同安。

translations.literal: Dingguo was defeated and fled; Chenggong again attacked Zhangzhou; Lieutenant Liu Guoxuan surrendered the city; advancing further, he again took Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo was beaten and fled. Chenggong then struck Zhangzhou; lieutenant Liu Guoxuan surrendered the city, and a further advance retook Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 其將甘輝陷仙遊，穴城入，殺掠殆盡。

translations.literal: His general Gan Hui took Xianyou, tunneled into the city, and killed and plundered nearly everyone.
translations.idiomatic: His general Gan Hui seized Xianyou, broke in through tunnels, and slaughtered and looted almost the entire population.

sentences.zh: 至是和議絕。

translations.literal: By then the peace talks had broken off.
translations.idiomatic: By then the peace negotiations were dead.

sentences.zh: 上命鄭親王世子濟度為定遠大將軍，率師討成功。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Prince Zheng's heir Jidu as General Who Pacifies the Distant and ordered him to lead the imperial army against Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Prince Zheng's heir Jidu General Who Pacifies the Distant and sent the imperial army to suppress Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 十二年，左都御史龔鼎孳請誅芝龍，國器亦發芝龍與成功私書，乃奪芝龍爵，下獄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Left Censor-in-Chief Gong Dingzi requested that Zhilong be executed; Guoqi also exposed private letters between Zhilong and Chenggong; Zhilong's title was then stripped and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Gong Dingzi, left censor-in-chief, urged Zhilong's execution; Guoqi also produced his private correspondence with Chenggong, and Zhilong was stripped of his rank and jailed.

sentences.zh: 成功遣其將洪旭、陳六禦攻陷舟山，進取溫、台，聞濟度師且至，隳安平鎮及漳州、惠安、南安、同安諸城，撤兵聚思明。

translations.literal: Chenggong sent his generals Hong Xu and Chen Liuyu to take Zhoushan and advance on Wenzhou and Taizhou; hearing that Jidu's army was approaching, he demolished Anping Fort and the cities of Zhangzhou, Huian, Nan'an, and Tong'an, withdrew his troops, and concentrated at Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong sent Hong Xu and Chen Liuyu to seize Zhoushan and push toward Wenzhou and Taizhou; when he learned Jidu's army was coming, he razed Anping and the Zhangzhou-area cities, pulled back, and massed at Siming.

sentences.zh: 濟度次泉州，檄招降，不納；

translations.literal: Jidu halted at Quanzhou and issued a summons to surrender, but they did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jidu camped at Quanzhou and called on them to surrender, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 易為書，成功依違答之。

translations.literal: The letter was rewritten, and Chenggong gave an equivocal reply.
translations.idiomatic: The summons was reworded, and Chenggong answered evasively.

sentences.zh: 上又令芝龍自獄中以書招成功，謂不降且族誅，成功終不應。

translations.literal: The emperor also had Zhilong write from prison to summon Chenggong, saying that if he did not surrender his whole clan would be executed; Chenggong still would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The court then had Zhilong write from prison, threatening the extermination of the clan if Chenggong would not submit; Chenggong never answered.

sentences.zh: 十三年，濟度以水師攻?門，成功遣其將林順、陳澤拒戰，颶起，師引還。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Jidu attacked Xiamen with the naval force; Chenggong sent his generals Lin Shun and Chen Ze to resist; a hurricane arose, and the imperial army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Jidu attacked Xiamen by sea; Chenggong sent Lin Shun and Chen Ze to meet him, but a typhoon rose and the imperial fleet fell back.

sentences.zh: 成功以軍儲置海澄，使王秀奇與黃梧、蘇明同守。

translations.literal: Chenggong stored military supplies at Haicheng and had Wang Xiuqi guard it together with Huang Wu and Su Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong stockpiled supplies at Haicheng and put Wang Xiuqi, Huang Wu, and Su Ming in joint command there.

sentences.zh: 梧先與明兄茂攻揭陽未克，成功殺茂，並責梧。

translations.literal: Wu had earlier joined Ming's elder brother Mao in an attack on Jieyang that failed; Chenggong executed Mao and also rebuked Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had earlier failed with Ming's brother Mao to take Jieyang; Chenggong killed Mao and blamed Wu as well.

sentences.zh: 梧、明並怨成功，俟秀奇出，以海澄降濟度。

translations.literal: Wu and Ming both resented Chenggong; when Xiuqi was away, they surrendered Haicheng to Jidu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Ming both nursed grievances against Chenggong; when Xiuqi was absent they handed Haicheng over to Jidu.

sentences.zh: 詔封梧海澄公，駐漳州，盡發鄭氏墓，斬成功所置官。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Wu as Duke of Haicheng and stationed him at Zhangzhou; the Zheng family tombs were all opened, and officials Chenggong had appointed were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was made Duke of Haicheng and posted to Zhangzhou; the Zheng tombs were desecrated and Chenggong's appointees were put to death.

sentences.zh: 大將軍伊爾德克舟山，擊殺六禦。

translations.literal: Grand General Irgen took Zhoushan and killed Liuyu in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Irgen captured Zhoushan and killed Chen Liuyu.

sentences.zh: 成功攻陷閩安城牛心塔，使陳斌戍焉。

translations.literal: Chenggong took the Niuxin Tower at Min'an city and had Chen Bin garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong seized the Niuxin Tower at Min'an and left Chen Bin to hold it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，鴻逵卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Hongkui died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Hongkui died.

sentences.zh: 師克閩安，斌降而殺之。

translations.literal: The imperial army took Min'an; Bin surrendered and was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army took Min'an; Chen Bin surrendered and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 成功陷台州。

translations.literal: Chenggong took Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong captured Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，謀大舉深入，與其將甘輝、餘新等率水師號十萬，陷樂清，遂破溫州，張煌言來會。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he planned a major thrust inland; with his generals Gan Hui, Yu Xin, and others he led a naval force said to number one hundred thousand, took Yueqing, then broke Wenzhou, and Zhang Huangyan came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he planned a deep inland campaign; with Gan Hui, Yu Xin, and others he led a fleet said to number one hundred thousand, seized Yueqing and Wenzhou, and Zhang Huangyan joined him.

sentences.zh: 將入江，次羊山，遇颶，舟敗，退泊舟山。

translations.literal: About to enter the Yangtze, they halted at Mount Yang; a hurricane struck, the ships were wrecked, and they withdrew to anchor at Zhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to enter the Yangtze they stopped at Mount Yang; a typhoon wrecked the fleet and they fell back to Zhoushan.

sentences.zh: 桂王使進封為王，成功辭，仍稱招討大將軍。

translations.literal: An envoy of the Gui Prince advanced to enfeoff him as king; Chenggong declined and still styled himself Pacification General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Gui Prince's envoy came to make him a king; Chenggong refused and kept the title Pacification General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月，成功率輝、新等整軍復出，次崇明，煌言來會，取瓜洲，攻鎮江，使煌言前驅，溯江上。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year Chenggong reorganized his army with Hui, Xin, and the others and set out again; he halted at Chongming; Huangyan came to join him; they took Guazhou and attacked Zhenjiang; Chenggong made Huangyan the vanguard and moved upriver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year Chenggong marched out again with Hui and Xin, camped at Chongming, and was joined by Huangyan; they took Guazhou, assaulted Zhenjiang, and sent Huangyan ahead up the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 提督管效忠師赴援，戰未合，成功將周全斌以所部陷陣，大雨，騎陷淖，成功兵徒跣擊刺，往來剽疾，效忠師敗績。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Guan Xiaozhong's army came to the rescue; before battle was joined, Chenggong's general Zhou Quanbin broke the enemy line with his unit; heavy rain mired the cavalry in mud; Chenggong's men fought barefoot with thrusting attacks, darting back and forth with fierce speed, and Xiaozhong's army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Guan Xiaozhong marched to relieve the city; before the armies fully engaged, Zhou Quanbin punched through with his own unit; in pouring rain the cavalry sank in mud while Chenggong's barefoot soldiers stabbed and slashed with startling speed, and Xiaozhong's force was routed.

sentences.zh: 成功入鎮江，將以違令斬全斌，繼而釋之，使守焉；

translations.literal: Chenggong entered Zhenjiang, was about to execute Quanbin for disobeying orders, then released him and had him hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong entered Zhenjiang, nearly executed Quanbin for insubordination, then spared him and left him to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 進攻江寧，煌言次蕪湖，廬、鳳、寧、徽、池、太諸府縣多與通款，騰書成功，謂宜收旁郡縣，以陸師急攻南京。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Jiangning; Huangyan halted at Wuhu; many prefectures and counties of Lu, Feng, Ning, Hui, Chi, and Tai opened communications; urgent letters reached Chenggong saying he ought to secure the surrounding prefectures and counties and press the land attack on Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on toward Jiangning while Huangyan held Wuhu; prefectures and counties across Lu, Feng, Ning, Hui, Chi, and Tai sent overtures; letters poured in urging Chenggong to secure the surrounding districts and storm Nanjing by land.

sentences.zh: 成功狃屢勝，方謁明太祖陵，會將吏置酒，輝諫不聽。

translations.literal: Chenggong, emboldened by repeated victories, was visiting the tomb of the Ming founding emperor and feasting with his officers; Hui remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with victory, Chenggong was visiting the tomb of the Ming founder and feasting with his commanders; Hui warned him in vain.

sentences.zh: 崇明總兵梁化鳳赴援，江甯總管喀喀木等合滿、漢兵出戰，襲破新軍，諸軍皆奔潰，遂大敗，生得輝猶數萬，棄瓜洲、鎮江，出海，欲取崇明。

translations.literal: Chongming garrison commander Liang Huafeng came to the rescue; Jiangning commandant Kekemu and others combined Manchu and Han troops for battle, struck and broke Xin's army, and all the forces fled in rout; the defeat was crushing; Gan Hui was captured alive, yet tens of thousands of men remained; they abandoned Guazhou and Zhenjiang, put to sea, and tried to take Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Huafeng of Chongming marched to help; Kekemu of Jiangning led combined Manchu and Han forces out, smashed Yu Xin's army, and routed the whole field; Gan Hui was taken alive, but Chenggong still had tens of thousands of men; he abandoned Guazhou and Zhenjiang, fled to sea, and tried to seize Chongming.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫蔣國柱遣兵赴援，化?殺之。

translations.literal: Jiangsu Governor Jiang Guozhu sent troops to the rescue, and Huafeng killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu governor Jiang Guozhu sent reinforcements, and Liang Huafeng cut them down.

sentences.zh: 成功收餘鳳亦還師禦之，成功戰復敗，引還。

translations.literal: Chenggong gathered his remaining forces; Huafeng also returned with his army to oppose him; Chenggong was defeated again in battle and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong regrouped what was left; Huafeng also turned back to meet him; Chenggong lost again and retreated.

sentences.zh: 煌言自間道走免。

translations.literal: Huangyan escaped by a hidden path.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan got away by a back trail.

sentences.zh: 上遣將軍達素、閩浙總督李率泰分兵出漳州、同安，規取?門。

translations.literal: The emperor sent General Daisu and Fujian-Zhejiang Governor-General Li Shuaitai to divide their forces out of Zhangzhou and Tong'an and plan the capture of Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent General Daisu and Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Li Shuaitai to advance from Zhangzhou and Tong'an with divided forces and take Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 成功使陳鵬守高崎，族兄泰出浯嶼，而與周全斌、陳輝、黃庭次海門。

translations.literal: Chenggong had Chen Peng hold Gaoqi; his clansman Tai moved out from Wuyu; while he himself with Zhou Quanbin, Chen Hui, and Huang Ting halted at Haimen.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong left Chen Peng at Gaoqi, sent his kinsman Tai out from Wuyu, and himself with Zhou Quanbin, Chen Hui, and Huang Ting took position at Haimen.

sentences.zh: 師自漳州薄海門戰，成功將周瑞、陳堯策死之，迫取輝舟，輝焚舟。

translations.literal: The imperial army pressed from Zhangzhou to fight at Haimen; Chenggong's generals Zhou Rui and Chen Yaoce were killed; they closed on Hui's ships, and Hui burned his vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army closed from Zhangzhou on Haimen; Zhou Rui and Chen Yaoce were killed; pressed hard, Chen Hui set his ships ablaze.

sentences.zh: 戰方急，風起，成功督巨艦沖入，泰亦自浯嶼引舟合擊，師大敗，有滿洲兵二百降，夜沈之海。

translations.literal: Battle was at its height when the wind rose; Chenggong drove great ships in; Tai also led boats from Wuyu in a combined strike; the imperial army was heavily defeated; two hundred Manchu soldiers surrendered and were drowned in the sea that night.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the fight the wind came up; Chenggong drove his great ships in and Tai swept from Wuyu in concert; the imperial fleet was smashed; two hundred Manchu troops surrendered and were sunk at sea that night.

sentences.zh: 師自同安鄉高崎，鵬約降。

translations.literal: The imperial army approached Gaoqi from Tong'an; Peng agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army moved on Gaoqi from Tong'an, and Peng agreed to defect.
