sentences.zh: 其部將陳蟒奮戰，師以鵬已降，不備，亦敗，成功收鵬殺之，引還。

translations.literal: His subordinate Chen Mang fought fiercely; the imperial army, thinking Peng had already surrendered, was unprepared and was also defeated; Chenggong recalled Peng and executed him, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Chen Mang fought hard; the imperial army, assuming Peng had already gone over, was caught off guard and beaten again; Chenggong pulled Peng back and had him executed, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命靖南王耿繼茂移鎮福建，又以羅讬為安南將軍，討成功。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the court ordered Prince of Pacifying the South Geng Jimaao to transfer his garrison to Fujian, and again appointed Luo Tuo General Who Pacifies Annam to suppress Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Prince of Pacifying the South Geng Jimaao was shifted to Fujian, and Luo Tuo was made General Who Pacifies Annam to campaign against Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，用黃梧議，徙濱海居民入內地，增兵守邊。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, following Huang Wu's proposal, coastal inhabitants were moved inland and border garrisons were strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, on Huang Wu's advice, coastal people were relocated inland and frontier garrisons were reinforced.

sentences.zh: 成功自江南敗還，知進取不易；

translations.literal: Chenggong returned defeated from the Jiangnan campaign and knew that further conquest would not be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong came back beaten from Jiangnan and saw that further advance would be hard.

sentences.zh: 桂王入緬甸，聲援絕，勢日蹙，乃規取臺灣。

translations.literal: The Gui Prince had entered Burma, outside support was cut off, and his position grew daily more desperate; he then planned to take Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: The Gui Prince had fled into Burma, outside support was gone, and the cause was collapsing; Chenggong then turned to seizing Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 臺灣，福建海中島，荷蘭紅毛人居之。

translations.literal: Taiwan was an island in the Fujian seas inhabited by the Dutch Red-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan was an island off Fujian held by the Dutch.

sentences.zh: 芝龍與顏思齊為盜時，嘗屯於此。

translations.literal: When Zhilong and Yan Siqi had been pirates, they had once encamped there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilong and Yan Siqi had once used it as a pirate base.

sentences.zh: 荷蘭築城二：曰赤嵌、曰王城，其海口曰鹿耳門。

translations.literal: The Dutch built two fortresses: one called Chiqian and one called the Royal City; the harbor mouth was called Luermen.
translations.idiomatic: The Dutch had built two forts, Chiqian and the Royal City, with Luermen as the harbor mouth.

sentences.zh: 荷蘭人恃鹿耳門水淺不可渡，不為備。

translations.literal: The Dutch relied on Luermen's shallow waters as impassable and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Dutch assumed Luermen's shoals were impassable and left them undefended.

sentences.zh: 成功師至，水驟長丈餘，舟大小銜尾徑進，紅毛人棄赤嵌走保王城。

translations.literal: When Chenggong's army arrived, the water suddenly rose more than a zhang; large and small boats entered in single file and pressed straight in; the Red-haired men abandoned Chiqian and fled to hold the Royal City.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong's force arrived, the tide surged more than ten feet; boats of every size filed in one after another; the Dutch abandoned Chiqian and fell back on the Royal City.

sentences.zh: 成功使謂之曰：「土地我故有，當還我；

translations.literal: Chenggong sent someone to tell them: "This land was originally ours; you must return it to us;
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong sent word: "This land was ours to begin with; give it back;

sentences.zh: 珍寶恣爾載歸。」

translations.literal: Take all the treasures you wish back with you."
translations.idiomatic: Take whatever treasure you like and go."

sentences.zh: 圍七閱月，紅毛存者僅百數十，城下，皆遣歸國。

translations.literal: End of quotation. After a siege of seven months, only about one hundred-odd Red-haired men remained; when the city fell, all were sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: End of quotation. The siege lasted seven months; only a little over a hundred Dutch remained; when the city fell, they were all sent home.

sentences.zh: 成功乃號臺灣為東都，示將迎桂王狩焉。

translations.literal: Chenggong then styled Taiwan the Eastern Capital, showing that he would welcome the Gui Prince there on a hunting tour.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong then called Taiwan the Eastern Capital, signaling that he would receive the Gui Prince there.

sentences.zh: 以陳永華為謀主，制法律，定職官，興學校。

translations.literal: He made Chen Yonghua his chief strategist, established laws, fixed the official ranks, and founded schools.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chen Yonghua his chief adviser, drew up laws, fixed the bureaucracy, and opened schools.

sentences.zh: 臺灣周千里，土地饒沃，招漳、泉、惠、潮四府民，辟草萊，興屯聚，令諸將移家實之。

translations.literal: Taiwan measured a thousand li around; the land was rich and fertile; he summoned people from the four prefectures of Zhang, Quan, Hui, and Chao, cleared wild fields, established military colonies, and ordered his generals to move their families there to settle it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan was a thousand li around and fertile; he drew settlers from Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, Huizhou, and Chaozhou, opened new fields, set up colonies, and ordered his generals to move their families there.

sentences.zh: 水土惡，皆憚行，又以令嚴不敢請，銅山守將郭義、蔡祿入漳州降。

translations.literal: The climate and water were harsh, and all feared to go; because the orders were strict none dared ask to stay; the Tongshan garrison commanders Guo Yi and Cai Lu entered Zhangzhou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was feared and the orders were strict, so few dared refuse; Guo Yi and Cai Lu, the Tongshan garrison commanders, went to Zhangzhou and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是歲，聖祖即位，戮芝龍及諸子世恩、世廕、世默。

translations.literal: That year the Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne and executed Zhilong and his sons Shi'en, Shiyin, and Shimo.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Kangxi Emperor came to the throne and executed Zhilong and his sons Shi'en, Shiyin, and Shimo.

sentences.zh: 成功既得臺灣，其將陳豹駐南澳，而令子錦居守思明。

translations.literal: Once Chenggong had secured Taiwan, his general Chen Bao garrisoned Nan'ao while he ordered his son Jin to remain and hold Siming.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Taiwan, Chenggong left Chen Bao at Nan'ao and put his son Jin in charge of Siming.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，成功聽周全斌讒，遣擊豹，豹舉軍入廣州降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, Chenggong listened to Zhou Quanbin's slander and sent troops to attack Bao; Bao led his whole army into Guangzhou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 Chenggong believed Zhou Quanbin's accusations and sent men against Chen Bao; Bao took his whole force to Guangzhou and submitted.

sentences.zh: 惡錦與乳媼通，生子，遣泰就殺錦及其母董。

translations.literal: He hated Jin for consorting with his wet nurse and fathering a child, and sent Tai to kill Jin and his mother, Lady Dong.
translations.idiomatic: He hated Jin for sleeping with his wet nurse and begetting a child, and sent Tai to kill Jin and his mother, Lady Dong.

sentences.zh: 會有訛言成功將盡殺諸將留?門者，值全斌自南澳還，執而囚之，擁錦，用芝龍初封，稱平國公，舉兵拒命。

translations.literal: Just then a rumor spread that Chenggong would kill all the generals left at Xiamen; when Quanbin returned from Nan'ao he was seized and imprisoned; the troops rallied to Jin, using Zhilong's original enfeoffment and styling him Duke of Pacifying the State, and raised arms in defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread that Chenggong meant to slaughter the generals left at Xiamen; Quanbin was seized on his return from Nan'ao; the men rallied to Jin, revived Zhilong's old title Duke of Pacifying the State, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 成功方病，聞之，狂怒咬指，五月朔，尚據胡?受諸將謁，數日遽卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: Chenggong was ill; when he heard this he flew into a rage and bit his finger; on the first day of the fifth month he still sat on a folding camp chair receiving the generals' visits, but within days he suddenly died at the age of thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong was already ill; hearing this he raged and bit his finger; on the first of the fifth month he still received his officers from a camp chair, but within days he was dead at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 成功子十，錦其長也，一名經。

translations.literal: Chenggong had ten sons; Jin was the eldest, also called Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong had ten sons; Jin was the eldest, also known as Jing.

sentences.zh: 成功既卒，臺灣諸將奉其幼弟世襲為招討大將軍，使，引兵至臺灣。

translations.literal: After Chenggong died, the Taiwan generals installed his younger brother Shixi as Pacification General-in-Chief, and Tai led troops to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong died, the Taiwan commanders made his younger brother Shixi Pacification General-in-Chief, and Tai marched to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 諸將有欲拒錦立?於錦告喪。

translations.literal: Some generals wished to resist Jin and install Shixi before Jin announced the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Some officers wanted to block Jin and put Shixi in power before Jin could announce the death.

sentences.zh: 錦出全斌使為將，以永華為諮議，馮錫範為侍世襲者，全斌力戰破之，錦乃入，嗣為延平王。

translations.literal: Jin released Quanbin and made him a general; he made Yonghua his counsellor and Feng Xifan attendant to Shixi; Quanbin fought hard and broke them; Jin then entered and succeeded as Prince of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Jin freed Quanbin and put him in command, made Yonghua counsellor and Feng Xifan Shixi's attendant; Quanbin fought through and broke the opposition; Jin then took power as Prince of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 世襲走泉州降。

translations.literal: Shixi fled to Quanzhou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shixi fled to Quanzhou and submitted.

sentences.zh: 二年，錦還思明。

translations.literal: In the second year Jin returned to Siming.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Jin went back to Siming.

sentences.zh: 泰嘗與臺灣諸將通書，錦得之，遂殺泰。

translations.literal: Tai had once exchanged letters with the Taiwan generals; Jin obtained them and then executed Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Tai had been corresponding with the Taiwan commanders; Jin got the letters and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 泰弟鳴駿、賡，子糸贊緒亦走泉州降。

translations.literal: Tai's younger brothers Mingjun and Geng and his son Zuanxu also fled to Quanzhou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's brothers Mingjun and Geng and his son Zuanxu also fled to Quanzhou and defected.

sentences.zh: 詔封鳴駿遵義侯、纘緒慕恩伯，世襲、賡皆授左都督。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Mingjun as Marquis of Zunyi and Zuanxu as Baron of Mu'en; Shixi and Geng were both appointed Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Mingjun was made Marquis of Zunyi and Zuanxu Baron of Mu'en; Shixi and Geng were both given the rank of left commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 諸將蔡鳴雷、陳輝、楊富、何義先後舉軍降。

translations.literal: The generals Cai Minglei, Chen Hui, Yang Fu, and He Yi successively led their armies in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Cai Minglei, Chen Hui, Yang Fu, and He Yi surrendered one after another with their forces.

sentences.zh: 錦漸弱。

translations.literal: Jin gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's position steadily weakened.

sentences.zh: 耿繼茂、李率泰大發兵規取金、?，出同安；

translations.literal: Geng Jimaao and Li Shuaitai mustered large forces to plan the capture of Jinmen and Xiamen and marched out of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jimaao and Li Shuaitai raised large armies to take Jinmen and Xiamen and advanced from Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 馬得功將降卒，並徵紅毛兵，出泉州；

translations.literal: Ma Degong led surrendered troops and also summoned Dutch forces, marching out of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Degong led defectors and Dutch auxiliaries out of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 黃梧、施琅出海澄。

translations.literal: Huang Wu and Shi Lang marched out of Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wu and Shi Lang moved out from Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 錦令全斌當得功，遇于金門外烏沙，得功舟三百，紅毛夾板船十四，全斌以二十舟入陣衝擊，紅毛?皆不中，諸舟披靡，得功戰死；

translations.literal: Jin ordered Quanbin to meet Degong; they encountered each other at Wusha outside Jinmen; Degong had three hundred boats and fourteen Dutch double-decked ships; Quanbin drove twenty boats into the line in a charge; the Dutch cannon shots all missed; the enemy vessels scattered; Degong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Quanbin against Ma Degong; they met at Wusha outside Jinmen; Degong had three hundred boats and fourteen Dutch men-of-war; Quanbin charged with twenty ships; the Dutch guns missed, the enemy line broke, and Degong was killed.

sentences.zh: 而同安、海澄二道兵大勝，直破?門。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the armies on the Tong'an and Haicheng routes won a great victory and broke straight through to Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Tong'an and Haicheng columns won a crushing victory and broke through to Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 琅復進克金門、浯嶼，錦退保銅山。

translations.literal: Lang then advanced and took Jinmen and Wuyu; Jin fell back to hold Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang then took Jinmen and Wuyu, and Jin withdrew to Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 三年，錦將杜輝以南澳降。

translations.literal: In the third year Jin's general Du Hui surrendered Nan'ao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Jin's general Du Hui gave up Nan'ao.

sentences.zh: 銅山糧垂盡，全斌亦出降，封承恩伯。

translations.literal: Tongshan's grain was nearly exhausted; Quanbin also came out and surrendered and was enfeoffed as Baron of Chengen.
translations.idiomatic: Tongshan was starving; Quanbin surrendered too and was made Baron of Chengen.

sentences.zh: 錦與其將黃廷堅守。

translations.literal: Jin and his general Huang Ting held on in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Huang Ting held out.

sentences.zh: 繼茂等復以水師出八尺門，廷與諸將翁求多等以三，載其孥盡入臺灣。

translations.literal: Jimaao and the others again sent the naval force out through Bachi Gate; Huang Ting and the generals Weng Qiuduo and others surrendered with thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jimaao again sent the fleet out through Bachi Gate; Huang Ting, Weng Qiuduo, and others surrendered with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 改東?萬人降，遂拔銅山，焚之，得仗艦無算。

translations.literal: Then Tongshan was taken, burned, and countless arms and warships were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tongshan was then taken and burned, and the victors seized arms and warships beyond count.

sentences.zh: 錦與永華及洪旭引餘都為東甯國，置天興、萬年二州，仍以永華綜國政。

translations.literal: Jin, Yonghua, and Hong Xu led the remaining forces, loaded their families entirely into Taiwan, renamed the Eastern Capital the Kingdom of Dongning, established the two prefectures of Tianxing and Wannian, and still had Yonghua manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Chen Yonghua, and Hong Xu withdrew with the rest, moved their families to Taiwan, renamed the Eastern Capital the Kingdom of Dongning, set up the Tianxing and Wannian prefectures, and left Yonghua in charge of government.

sentences.zh: 詔授施琅靖海將軍，周全斌、楊富為副，督水師攻臺灣，阻颶，不得進。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shi Lang Pacification General of the Sea, with Zhou Quanbin and Yang Fu as deputies, to command the naval force in an attack on Taiwan; a hurricane blocked them and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang was made Pacification General of the Sea, with Zhou Quanbin and Yang Fu as deputies, to attack Taiwan by sea, but a typhoon stopped them.

sentences.zh: 四年，廷議罷兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the court debated halting the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the court debated calling off the war.

sentences.zh: 李率泰請遣知府慕天顏諭降，假卿銜，齎敕往。

translations.literal: Li Shuaitai requested that Prefect Mu Tianyan be sent to summon surrender, granted a provisional ministerial title, and dispatched with an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuaitai asked that prefect Mu Tianyan be sent with a temporary ministerial title and an imperial edict to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 錦請稱臣入貢如朝鮮，上未之許。

translations.literal: Jin asked to declare himself a subject and send tribute like Korea; the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin offered to submit and pay tribute like Korea; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵琅入京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Lang was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shi Lang was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 撤降兵分屯諸省，嚴戍守界，不復以臺灣為意。

translations.literal: Surrendered troops were withdrawn and stationed in the provinces; border defenses were tightened; Taiwan was no longer a priority.
translations.idiomatic: Defector troops were posted across the provinces, the frontier was tightened, and Taiwan ceased to be a focus.

sentences.zh: 錦兵亦不出。

translations.literal: Jin's troops also did not venture out.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's forces stayed put as well.

sentences.zh: 相安者數年，濱海居民漸復業。

translations.literal: Peace held for several years, and coastal inhabitants gradually returned to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides kept the peace for years, and coastal people slowly resumed their lives.

sentences.zh: 十二年，耿精忠將以福建叛應吳三桂，使約錦為援。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Geng Jingzhong was about to rebel in Fujian in response to Wu Sangui and sent to enlist Jin as an ally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Geng Jingzhong prepared to rebel in Fujian with Wu Sangui and sent to win Jin as an ally.

sentences.zh: 十三年，精忠遂反，錦仍稱永歷年號。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Jingzhong rebelled; Jin still used the Yongli reign title.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Jingzhong rose; Jin kept the Yongli reign title.

sentences.zh: 以永華輔長子克𡒉居守，與諸將馮錫范等督諸軍渡海而西，入思明，取同安。

translations.literal: He left Yonghua to assist his eldest son Kezang in holding the home base, and with the generals Feng Xifan and others directed the armies across the sea westward, entered Siming, and took Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yonghua with his eldest son Kezang to hold Taiwan, and with Feng Xifan and others led the army west across the sea into Siming and took Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 錦以族人省英知思明，省英，芝筦子也。

translations.literal: Jin appointed his clansman Sheng Ying to administer Siming; Sheng Ying was Zhima's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jin put his kinsman Sheng Ying in charge of Siming; Sheng Ying was Zhima's son.

sentences.zh: 集舟航，整部伍，方引軍復出，而精忠與爭泉州。

translations.literal: He gathered boats, reorganized the ranks, and was just leading the army out again when Jingzhong also contested Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered ships, reformed his ranks, and was marching out again when Jingzhong also moved on Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 泉州兵內亂，精忠所遣守將潰圍走，迎錦師入，復攻下漳州。

translations.literal: The Quanzhou garrison mutinied; the defending commander Jingzhong had sent broke out and fled, welcomed Jin's army in, and again attacked and took Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou's garrison mutinied; Jingzhong's commander broke out and fled, let Jin's army in, and they took Zhangzhou again.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣兵圍潮州，潮州總兵劉進忠降於錦，錦遣其將趙得勝入潮州，擊破精忠兵。

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent troops to besiege Chaozhou; Chaozhou garrison commander Liu Jinzhong surrendered to Jin; Jin sent his general Zhao Desheng into Chaozhou and defeated Jingzhong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong besieged Chaozhou; Liu Jinzhong, the Chaozhou commander, went over to Jin; Jin sent Zhao Desheng into Chaozhou and routed Jingzhong's force.

sentences.zh: 錦更定軍制，以錫范及參軍陳繩武贊畫諸政，諸將劉國軒、薛進思、何祐、許輝、施福、艾禎祥分領各軍。

translations.literal: Jin reorganized the military system, making Xifan and staff officer Chen Shengwu planners of all affairs, and assigning the generals Liu Guoxuan, Xue Jinsi, He You, Xu Hui, Shi Fu, and Ai Zhenxiang to command the separate armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jin reorganized the army, put Xifan and staff officer Chen Shengwu in charge of planning, and gave Liu Guoxuan, Xue Jinsi, He You, Xu Hui, Shi Fu, and Ai Zhenxiang separate commands.

sentences.zh: 省英為宣慰使，督各郡錢糧，令人月輸銀五分，曰「毛丁」；

translations.literal: Sheng Ying was made Pacification Commissioner, supervising money and grain in all prefectures; he required each person to pay five fen of silver per month, called the "Maoding" levy;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Ying was appointed Pacification Commissioner to oversee money and grain in every prefecture; each person was taxed five fen of silver monthly, a levy called "Maoding";

sentences.zh: 船計丈尺輸稅，曰「樑頭」。

translations.literal: Ships were taxed by length and beam, called the "Liangtou" levy.
translations.idiomatic: Ships were taxed by their length and beam, a levy called "Liangtou."

sentences.zh: 鹽司分筦鹽場，鹽石值二錢，徵餉四錢；

translations.literal: The salt office divided administration of the salt fields; salt worth two cash per picul was levied at four cash for supplies;
translations.idiomatic: The salt office took charge of the salt fields; though salt was worth two cash per picul, four cash was collected for rations;

sentences.zh: 餉司科雜稅給軍。

translations.literal: The commissariat office assessed miscellaneous taxes to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The commissariat office levied assorted taxes to pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 復開互市，英圭黎、暹羅、安南諸國市舶並至，思明井裏?火幾如承平時。

translations.literal: The frontier market was reopened; merchant ships from England, Siam, Annam, and other countries all arrived; lamps in the streets and lanes of Siming were nearly as before in peacetime.
translations.idiomatic: Border trade resumed; trading vessels from England, Siam, Annam, and elsewhere all put in; the lights of Siming's lanes burned almost as they had in peaceful days.

sentences.zh: 十四年，精忠使賀年，錦亦報禮，自是復相結。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Jingzhong sent envoys with New Year greetings; Jin returned the courtesy; from then on they allied again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Jingzhong sent New Year's greetings; Jin sent gifts in return, and the two were allied once more.

sentences.zh: 永春民呂花，保所居村曰「馬跳」，不應徵索，使進忠圍之，三月不下，誘花降而殺之。

translations.literal: A Yongchun man named Lü Hua defended his village, called "Matiao," and refused levies; Jin sent Jinzhong to besiege it; after three months it did not fall; he lured Hua into surrender and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hua of Yongchun held his village, called Matiao, and refused exactions; Jin sent Jinzhong to besiege it; three months failed to take it; Hua was tricked into surrender and killed.

sentences.zh: 續順公沈瑞屯饒平，進忠攻之，何祐擊破援兵，遂執瑞及其孥歸於臺灣。

translations.literal: The Continuation Duke of Shun, Shen Rui, was stationed at Raoping; Jinzhong attacked him; He You defeated the relief force; he then seized Rui and his family and took them to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Rui, Prince of Continuation Shun, was posted at Raoping; Jinzhong attacked him; He You smashed the relief force and carried Rui and his family off to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 海澄公黃梧卒，子芳度保漳州。

translations.literal: The Duke of Haicheng, Huang Wu, died; his son Fangdu held Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wu, Duke of Haicheng, died; his son Fangdu kept hold of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦自海澄移軍萬松關，祐亦自潮州攻平和，降守將賴升。

translations.literal: Jin moved his army from Haicheng to Wansong Pass; You also attacked Pinghe from Chaozhou and reduced the defending general Lai Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin shifted his army from Haicheng to Wansong Pass; You marched from Chaozhou on Pinghe and won over the defender Lai Sheng.

sentences.zh: 芳度孤守漳州，圍合，總兵吳淑以城降，芳度死之，其孥皆殉。

translations.literal: Fangdu alone defended Zhangzhou; the encirclement closed; garrison commander Wu Shu surrendered the city; Fangdu died in the fight; his family all perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdu held Zhangzhou alone; the ring closed; Wu Shu, the garrison commander, surrendered the city; Fangdu died fighting, and his family perished with him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，康親王傑書下福建，精忠降，克泉州，國軒復圍之，兩月不下。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Prince Kang Jieshu entered Fujian; Jingzhong surrendered; Quanzhou was taken; Guo Xuan besieged it again; two months passed without its fall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Prince Kang Jieshu marched into Fujian; Jingzhong surrendered and Quanzhou fell; Guo Xuan besieged it again but could not take it in two months.

sentences.zh: 李光地迎師自間道赴援，總兵林賢、黃鎬、樸子威以舟師會，國軒退次長泰，隳同安，稍進屯漳州溪西。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi welcomed the imperial army by a hidden route to relieve the city; garrison commanders Lin Xian, Huang Hao, and Pu Ziwei joined with the fleet; Guo Xuan withdrew to Changtai, destroyed Tong'an, and advanced gradually to camp west of the Zhangzhou stream.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi brought the Qing army by a back road to the rescue; Lin Xian, Huang Hao, and Pu Ziwei united their fleets; Guo Xuan fell back to Changtai, razed Tong'an, and slowly encamped west of Zhangzhou creek.

sentences.zh: 師進擊國軒，國軒敗，棄長泰走。

translations.literal: The imperial army advanced and attacked Guo Xuan; Guo Xuan was defeated, abandoned Changtai, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army pressed Guo Xuan; he was beaten, abandoned Changtai, and fled.

sentences.zh: 錦將許輝以二萬人攻福州，壁烏龍江。

translations.literal: Jin's general Xu Hui attacked Fuzhou with twenty thousand men and fortified at Wulong River.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's general Xu Hui marched twenty thousand men on Fuzhou and entrenched at the Wulong River.

sentences.zh: 康親王遣副都統喇哈達等渡江奮擊，破其壘，逐北四十里。

translations.literal: Prince Kang sent Vice Commander-in-chief Lahada and others to cross the river and fight fiercely; they broke the stockade and pursued north for forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang sent Lahada and other vice commanders across the river; they stormed the camp and chased the enemy forty li north.

sentences.zh: 興、泉、汀、漳諸郡盡復，惟海澄未下。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Xinghua, Quanzhou, Tingzhou, and Zhangzhou were all recovered; only Haicheng remained untaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua, Quanzhou, Tingzhou, and Zhangzhou were all back in Qing hands; only Haicheng still held out.

sentences.zh: 十六年，師克海澄，錦復破之，遂圍泉州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the imperial army took Haicheng; Jin recaptured it, then besieged Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Qing army took Haicheng; Jin seized it back and laid siege to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦下教?國軒、淑、祐等功。

translations.literal: Jin issued promotion orders commending Guo Xuan, Shu, You, and others for their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jin issued edicts of commendation for Guo Xuan, Wu Shu, He You, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 副都統穆赫林等克泰甯、建甯、寧化、長汀、清流、歸化、連城、上杭、武平、永定，凡十縣。

translations.literal: Vice Commander-in-chief Mu Helin and others took Taining, Jianning, Ninghua, Changting, Qingliu, Guihua, Liancheng, Shanghang, Wuping, and Yongding—ten counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin and other vice commanders captured Taining, Jianning, Ninghua, Changting, Qingliu, Guihua, Liancheng, Shanghang, Wuping, and Yongding—ten counties in all.

sentences.zh: 喇哈達等解泉州圍，錦撤兵還思明。

translations.literal: Lahada and others lifted the siege of Quanzhou; Jin withdrew his troops to Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Lahada lifted the siege of Quanzhou; Jin pulled his army back to Siming.

sentences.zh: 十七年，康親王遣知府張仲舉招錦，不納。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Prince Kang sent prefect Zhang Zhongju to summon Jin; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Prince Kang sent Prefect Zhang Zhongju to win Jin over; Jin refused.

sentences.zh: 國軒自長泰退據三汊河、玉洲、水頭、鎮門諸寨，屢遣兵攻石瑪、江東橋。

translations.literal: Guo Xuan withdrew from Changtai and held the camps at Sancha River, Yuzhou, Shuitou, and Zhenmen; he repeatedly sent troops to attack Shima and Jiangdong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan fell back from Changtai to camps at Sancha River, Yuzhou, Shuitou, and Zhenmen, and repeatedly struck at Shima and Jiangdong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 錦又遣其將林耀、林英犯泉州，提督段應舉擊破之，獲耀。

translations.literal: Jin again sent his generals Lin Yao and Lin Ying to raid Quanzhou; Grand Coordinator Duan Yingju defeated them and captured Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin again sent Lin Yao and Lin Ying against Quanzhou; Duan Yingju, the grand coordinator, routed them and took Yao prisoner.

sentences.zh: 吳淑又自石瑪登陸，海澄公黃芳世、都統孟安擊破之，沈其舟。

translations.literal: Wu Shu again landed from Shima; the Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangshi and Commander-in-chief Meng An defeated him and sank his boats.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shu landed again from Shima; Huang Fangshi, Duke of Haicheng, and Commander Meng An broke him and sent his boats to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 上令復徙濱海民如順治十八年例，遷界守邊。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered coastal people again moved inland as in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi; the boundary was reset to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered coastal people relocated inland as in Shunzhi 18, shifting the frontier to tighten the border.

sentences.zh: 穆赫林、黃芳世會師灣腰樹，攻國軒，師敗績。

translations.literal: Mu Helin and Huang Fangshi united their armies at Wanyao Tree and attacked Guo Xuan; the imperial army suffered a defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin and Huang Fangshi joined forces at Wanyao Tree and attacked Guo Xuan; the Qing army was badly beaten.

sentences.zh: 國軒陷平和、漳平，遂復破海澄，段應舉、穆赫林及總兵黃藍死之。

translations.literal: Guo Xuan took Pinghe and Zhangping, then broke Haicheng again; Duan Yingju, Mu Helin, and garrison commander Huang Lan died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan took Pinghe and Zhangping, then retook Haicheng; Duan Yingju, Mu Helin, and Huang Lan, a garrison commander, were killed.

sentences.zh: 藍，梧族，芳度所遣詣京師奏事者也。

translations.literal: Lan was of Huang Wu's clan; Fangdu had sent him to the capital to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lan was Huang Wu's kinsman, whom Fangdu had sent to the capital on official business.

sentences.zh: 國軒進圍泉州。

translations.literal: Guo Xuan advanced to besiege Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan pressed the siege of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔趣諸軍合擊，將軍喇哈達、賴塔，總督姚啟聖，巡撫吳興祚，提督楊捷，分道並進，賢、鎬、子威以舟師會，克平和、漳平、惠安，復解泉州圍。

translations.literal: An edict urged the armies to unite in attack; General Lahada, Laita, Governor-General Yao Qisheng, Provincial Governor Wu Xingzuo, and Grand Coordinator Yang Jie advanced on separate routes; Xian, Hao, and Ziwei joined with the fleet; they took Pinghe, Zhangping, and Hui'an and again lifted the siege of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a combined assault; Lahada, Laita, Yao Qisheng, Wu Xingzuo, and Yang Jie advanced by separate routes; Lin Xian, Huang Hao, and Pu Ziwei brought up the fleet; Pinghe, Zhangping, and Hui'an fell, and the siege of Quanzhou was broken.

sentences.zh: 啟聖與賴塔等逐國軒至長泰，及於蜈蚣山，大破之，斬四千餘級，進克同安，斬錦將林欽。

translations.literal: Qisheng and Laita and others chased Guo Xuan to Changtai and caught him at Wugong Mountain; they routed him and beheaded more than four thousand; they advanced and took Tong'an and beheaded Jin's general Lin Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng and Laita chased Guo Xuan to Changtai and caught him at Wugong Mountain; more than four thousand heads were taken; Tong'an fell, and Jin's general Lin Qin was killed.

sentences.zh: 賴塔又破錦兵萬松關，啟聖、捷及副都統吉勒塔布等，與國軒戰于江東橋、於潮溝，國軒屢敗。

translations.literal: Laita again broke Jin's army at Wansong Pass; Qisheng, Jie, and Vice Commander-in-chief Jiletabu and others fought Guo Xuan at Jiangdong Bridge and Chao Gou; Guo Xuan was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Laita broke Jin's force at Wansong Pass; Qisheng, Yang Jie, Jiletabu, and others fought Guo Xuan at Jiangdong Bridge and Chao Gou and beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 副都統瑚圖又擊吳淑于石街，盡焚其舟。

translations.literal: Vice Commander-in-chief Hutu again attacked Wu Shu at Shijie and burned all his boats.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu struck Wu Shu at Shijie and burned every boat he had.

sentences.zh: 錦斂兵退保思明。

translations.literal: Jin gathered his troops and withdrew to hold Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Jin gathered his army and fell back to Siming.

sentences.zh: 詔厚集舟師，規取金、?。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a large fleet assembled to plan the capture of Jinmen and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for a great fleet to take Jinmen and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 十九年，興祚出同安，與啟聖、捷會師，自陸路鄉?門。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Xingzuo marched out of Tong'an, joined Qisheng and Jie, and by land route pressed toward Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Wu Xingzuo left Tong'an, joined Qisheng and Yang Jie, and marched overland on Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 提督萬正色以水師攻海壇，分兵為六隊前進，自統巨艦繼；

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wan Zhengse attacked Haitan with the fleet, divided his troops into six columns to advance, and himself followed in a great ship;
translations.idiomatic: Wan Zhengse, the grand coordinator, attacked Haitan by sea in six columns, following in his flagship;

sentences.zh: 又以輕舟繞出左右，發砲毀錦師船十六，兵三千餘入水死，錦將硃天貴引退。

translations.literal: He also sent light boats around both flanks, opened fire and destroyed sixteen of Jin's ships; more than three thousand soldiers drowned; Jin's general Zhu Tiangui withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Light craft flanked both sides; cannon fire sank sixteen of Jin's ships and drowned more than three thousand men; Zhu Tiangui, a Jin general, pulled back.

sentences.zh: 正色督兵追擊，斬錦將吳內、林勳。

translations.literal: Zhengse directed the troops in pursuit and beheaded Jin's generals Wu Nei and Lin Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse pressed the pursuit and killed Jin's generals Wu Nei and Lin Xun.

sentences.zh: 湄洲、南日、平海、崇武諸澳皆下。

translations.literal: The harbors of Meizhou, Nanri, Pinghai, and Chongwu all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Meizhou, Nanri, Pinghai, and Chongwu all fell.

sentences.zh: 天貴出降。

translations.literal: Tiangui came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tiangui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 副都統沃申擊破錦將林英、張志，水陸並進，趨玉洲，國軒走還思明。

translations.literal: Vice Commander-in-chief Woshen defeated Jin's generals Lin Ying and Zhang Zhi; land and sea forces advanced together toward Yuzhou; Guo Xuan fled back to Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Woshen routed Jin's generals Lin Ying and Zhang Zhi; land and sea columns advanced on Yuzhou; Guo Xuan fled to Siming.

sentences.zh: 錦將蘇堪以海澄降。

translations.literal: Jin's general Su Kan surrendered Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan, a Jin general, surrendered Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 啟聖分遣總兵趙得壽、黃大來從賴塔擊破陳洲、馬洲、灣腰山、觀音山、黃旗諸寨。

translations.literal: Qisheng separately sent garrison commanders Zhao Deshou and Huang Dalai with Laita to break the camps at Chenzhou, Mazhou, Wanyao Mountain, Guanyin Mountain, and Huangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng sent Zhao Deshou and Huang Dalai with Laita to storm the camps at Chenzhou, Mazhou, Wanyao Mountain, Guanyin Mountain, and Huangqi.

sentences.zh: 興祚復與喇哈達等逐錦兵至潯尾，遂克?門、金門，錦還臺灣。

translations.literal: Xingzuo again with Lahada and others drove Jin's army to Xunwei, then took Xiamen and Jinmen; Jin returned to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingzuo and Lahada drove Jin's troops to Xunwei and took Xiamen and Jinmen; Jin withdrew to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，錦卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Jin died.

sentences.zh: 子克𡒉（

translations.literal: His son Kezang (
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kezang (

sentences.zh: 𡒉，為鄭經庶出長子），

translations.literal: [Ke]zhao, the eldest son born to Zheng Jin by a concubine),
translations.idiomatic: Kezhao, Jin's eldest son by a concubine)

sentences.zh: 自錦出師時為居守，永華請於錦，號「監國」。

translations.literal: from the time Jin took the field had held the home base; Yonghua petitioned Jin that he be styled "Regent of the State."
translations.idiomatic: had stayed behind when Jin marched out; Yonghua asked Jin to style him "Regent of the State."

sentences.zh: 年未冠，明察能治事，顧乳媼子錫範等意不屬，先構罷永華兵，永華鬱鬱死；

translations.literal: Though not yet capped, he was perceptive and able to govern; yet Feng Xifan, a wet nurse's son, and others did not set their hearts on him; they first contrived to strip Yonghua of his command; Yonghua died in gloom;
translations.idiomatic: Though still under age, he was sharp and capable; but Feng Xifan, the wet nurse's son, and others looked elsewhere; they first stripped Yonghua of his troops; Yonghua died broken-hearted;

sentences.zh: 及錦卒，遂共縊殺克𡒉，奉錦次子克塽嗣為延平王。

translations.literal: When Jing died they jointly strangled Kezang and installed Jing's second son Ke Shuang as Prince of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing died they strangled Kezang and put Jing's second son Ke Shuang on the throne as Prince of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 克塽幼弱，事皆決于錫範。

translations.literal: Ke Shuang was young and weak; all affairs were decided by Xifan.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shuang was young; Xifan decided everything.

sentences.zh: 行人傅為霖謀合諸將從中起，事泄，錫範執而殺之，並及續順公沈瑞。

translations.literal: The Bearer of Dispatches Fu Weilin plotted with the generals to rise from within; the affair leaked; Xifan seized and killed him, and Shen Rui, Prince of Continuation Shun, was implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Weilin, Bearer of Dispatches, plotted a coup with the generals; the plot leaked; Xifan had him seized and killed, and Shen Rui, Prince of Continuation Shun, died with him.

sentences.zh: 詔用施琅為水師提督，與啟聖規取臺灣。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shi Lang Grand Coordinator of the Fleet and with Qisheng planned the capture of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Lang was made grand coordinator of the fleet to plan Taiwan's capture with Qisheng.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，國軒投書啟聖，復請稱臣入貢視琉球。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Guo Xuan sent a letter to Qisheng again asking to submit as a vassal and pay tribute like Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Guo Xuan wrote Qisheng again, offering vassalage and tribute on the Ryukyu model.

sentences.zh: 上趣琅進兵。

translations.literal: The emperor urged Lang to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lang to march.

sentences.zh: 時國軒以二萬人守澎湖。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Xuan held Penghu with twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan held Penghu with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 六月，琅師乘南風發銅山，入八罩嶼，攻澎湖，擊沈錦師船二百，斬將吏三百七十有奇、兵萬餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Lang's fleet caught the south wind from Tongshan, entered Bazhao Isle, attacked Penghu, sank two hundred of Jin's ships, and beheaded more than three hundred seventy officers and over ten thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Lang's fleet rode the south wind from Tongshan to Bazhao and struck Penghu; two hundred of Jin's ships went down, more than three hundred seventy officers were killed, and over ten thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 國軒以小舟自吼門走臺灣。

translations.literal: Guo Xuan escaped in a small boat through Haimen to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan fled through Haimen in a small boat to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 七月吳啟爵持榜入臺灣諭軍民薙發?，克塽使請降，琅疏聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wu Qijue entered Taiwan with a proclamation urging soldiers and civilians to shave their heads; Ke Shuang sent envoys to surrender; Lang memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wu Qijue entered Taiwan with a proclamation ordering the people to shave their heads; Ke Shuang sent to surrender; Lang reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上降敕宣撫，克塽上降表，琅遣侍。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a pacification edict; Ke Shuang submitted a surrender memorial; Lang sent attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a pacification edict; Ke Shuang submitted his surrender; Lang dispatched attendants.

sentences.zh: 八月，琅督兵至鹿耳門，水淺不得入，泊十有二日，潮驟長高丈餘，?舟平入。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Lang led his troops to Lu'ermen; the water was too shallow to enter; they anchored twelve days; the tide suddenly rose more than a zhang; the fleet of boats entered on the level water.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lang reached Lu'ermen but could not enter for the shoals; after twelve days at anchor the tide surged more than a zhang; the whole fleet rode it in.

sentences.zh: 臺灣人鹹驚，謂無異成功初至時也。

translations.literal: The people of Taiwan were all amazed, saying it was no different from when Chenggong first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Taiwan were stunned—it was as if Chenggong had arrived again.

sentences.zh: 克塽及國軒、錫范率諸將吏出降，詣京師，上授克塽公爵，隸漢軍正紅旗，國軒、錫范皆伯爵。

translations.literal: Ke Shuang, Guo Xuan, and Xifan led the officers and officials out to surrender and went to the capital; the emperor granted Ke Shuang the rank of duke and enrolled him in the Plain Red Banner of the Chinese Bordered Eight Banners; Guo Xuan and Xifan were both made earls.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shuang, Guo Xuan, and Xifan surrendered with their officers and went to the capital; Ke Shuang was made a duke and enrolled in the Plain Red Banner; Guo Xuan and Xifan were made earls.

sentences.zh: 諸明宗人依鄭氏者，甯靖王術桂自殺，魯王子及他宗室皆徙河南。

translations.literal: Among Ming imperial clansmen who had relied on the Zheng house, Prince Ningjing Zhu Shugui killed himself; the Prince of Lu's son and other members of the imperial clan were all moved to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming princes who had thrown in with the Zhengs followed their fate: Prince Ningjing Zhu Shugui took his own life; the Prince of Lu's son and other royals were sent to Henan.

sentences.zh: 上以國軒為天津總兵，召對慰勉。

translations.literal: The emperor made Guo Xuan garrison commander of Tianjin and summoned him for audience with words of comfort and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan was made garrison commander of Tianjin and summoned for a comforting audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 眷屬至，賜第京師。

translations.literal: When his dependents arrived, a residence in the capital was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his family arrived, the court gave him a house in the capital.

sentences.zh: 克塽請為成功子聰、錦子克舉等?官，上特許之。

translations.literal: Ke Shuang asked that offices be granted to Chenggong's son Cong, Jin's son Keju, and others; the emperor specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shuang asked offices for Chenggong's son Cong, Jin's son Keju, and others; the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，德宗允船政大臣沈葆楨疏請，為成功立祠臺灣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign Emperor Dezong granted the petition of Director-General of the Naval Construction Bureau Shen Baozhen and established a shrine to Chenggong in Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, Emperor Dezong granted Shen Baozhen's request and had a shrine to Chenggong built in Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 李定國，字鴻遠，陝西延安人。

translations.literal: Li Dingguo, style name Hongyuan, was a native of Yan'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo, styled Hongyuan, came from Yan'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初從張獻忠為亂，與孫可望、劉文秀、艾能奇並為獻忠養子。

translations.literal: At first he followed Zhang Xianzhong in rebellion; with Sun Kewang, Liu Wenxiu, and Ai Nengqi he was alike adopted as Xianzhong's son.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Zhang Xianzhong in revolt; he and Sun Kewang, Liu Wenxiu, and Ai Nengqi were all Xianzhong's adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 獻忠入四川，遣諸將分道屠殺，定國為撫南將軍。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong entered Sichuan he sent his generals on separate routes to slaughter; Dingguo was made Pacifier of the South General.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong entered Sichuan he sent generals on killing sweeps; Dingguo was made Pacifier of the South.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，肅親王豪格率師入四川，獻忠死西充，可望與定國等及白文選、馮雙禮率殘眾自重慶而南，四年，破遵義，入貴州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi Prince Su Haoge led the imperial army into Sichuan; Xianzhong died at Xichong; Kewang with Dingguo and others and Bai Wenxuan and Feng Shuangli led the remnant force south from Chongqing; in the fourth year they took Zunyi and entered Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 Prince Su Haoge marched into Sichuan; Xianzhong died at Xichong; Kewang, Dingguo, Bai Wenxuan, and Feng Shuangli led the survivors south from Chongqing; in the fourth year they took Zunyi and entered Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 可望令定國襲破臨安，屠其城，盡下迤東諸郡縣，定國等皆自號為王。

translations.literal: Kewang ordered Dingguo to raid and take Lin'an, slaughtered the city, and brought all the southeastern prefectures and counties under submission; Dingguo and the others all styled themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang sent Dingguo to storm Lin'an and sack it; the southeastern prefectures fell; Dingguo and the rest each proclaimed himself king.

sentences.zh: 居年餘，可望用任僎議，自號為國主。

translations.literal: After more than a year Kewang followed Ren Fu's counsel and styled himself lord of the state.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Kewang took Ren Fu's advice and styled himself lord of the state.

sentences.zh: 時能奇已前卒，定國、文秀故儕輩，不相下，而定國尤崛強。

translations.literal: By then Nengqi had already died earlier; Dingguo and Wenxiu were old peers and would not yield to each other; Dingguo was especially obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Nengqi was already dead; Dingguo and Wenxiu, old equals, would not bow to each other; Dingguo was the most unyielding.

sentences.zh: 六年春，可望密與文秀謀，藉演武聲定國罪，縛而杖之百。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Kewang secretly plotted with Wenxiu; using a military review as pretext he proclaimed Dingguo's crimes, bound him, and flogged him a hundred blows.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year Kewang secretly colluded with Wenxiu; at a field review he condemned Dingguo, bound him, and gave him a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 已，復相抱哭，令取沙定洲自贖。

translations.literal: Afterwards they again embraced and wept, and he ordered Dingguo to redeem himself by taking Sha Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then they embraced and wept; Kewang ordered Dingguo to redeem himself by capturing Sha Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 定國憾可望，念兄事久，未可遽發難，乃率所部攻定洲，定洲降械以歸，剝皮死。

translations.literal: Dingguo resented Kewang but, remembering their long brotherhood, could not quickly raise trouble; he therefore led his troops to attack Dingzhou; Dingzhou surrendered stripped of arms and was brought back; he was flayed alive.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo resented Kewang but, bound by years as sworn brothers, would not rebel yet; he marched on Dingzhou; Sha Dingzhou surrendered unarmed and was brought back and flayed alive.

sentences.zh: 定國兵漸強。

translations.literal: Dingguo's army gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo's army grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 可望知不可制，乃通使桂王，思得封爵，彈壓諸將。

translations.literal: Kewang knew he could not control him, so he sent envoys to the Gui prince, hoping to gain enfeoffment and pressure the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang saw he could not control Dingguo and sent envoys to the Gui prince, seeking a title to hold the generals in check.

sentences.zh: 桂王封可望公，尋進為王。

translations.literal: The Gui prince enfeoffed Kewang as duke, and soon after advanced him to prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Gui prince made Kewang a duke, then a prince.

sentences.zh: 定國與文秀亦自侯進公。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu also rose from marquis to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu were promoted from marquis to duke.

sentences.zh: 八年，可望遣使迎桂王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Kewang sent envoys to welcome the Gui prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Kewang sent to bring the Gui prince.

sentences.zh: 九年，劫遷安隆所。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he seized and moved him to Anlong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he moved the court by force to Anlong.

sentences.zh: 會定南王孔有德師出河池向貴州，可望令定國與馮雙禮將八萬人自黎平出靖州，別遣馬進忠自鎮遠出沅州，兩軍會武岡，圖桂林。

translations.literal: When Prince Dingnan Kong Youde led his army out of Hechi toward Guizhou, Kewang ordered Dingguo and Feng Shuangli to lead eighty thousand men from Liping toward Jingzhou; he separately sent Ma Jinzhong from Zhenyuan toward Yuanzhou; the two armies were to meet at Wugang and aim at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dingnan Kong Youde marched from Hechi toward Guizhou, Kewang sent Dingguo and Feng Shuangli with eighty thousand men from Liping toward Jingzhou and Ma Jinzhong from Zhenyuan toward Yuanzhou; the two columns were to join at Wugang and take Guilin.

sentences.zh: 文秀亦出兵規取成都。

translations.literal: Wenxiu also sent troops planning to take Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu also marched to take Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 可望言於桂王，進定國西寧王、文秀南康王。

translations.literal: Kewang spoke to the Gui prince and had Dingguo advanced to Prince of Xining and Wenxiu to Prince of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang persuaded the Gui prince to make Dingguo Prince of Xining and Wenxiu Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 定國自靖州進陷沅州，再進，陷寶慶，遂破武岡，與雙禮兵合。

translations.literal: Dingguo advanced from Jingzhou and took Yuanzhou; advancing again he took Baoqing, then broke Wugang, and joined Feng Shuangli's army.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo marched from Jingzhou and took Yuanzhou, then Baoqing, then Wugang, and joined Feng Shuangli.

sentences.zh: 有德引師還桂林。

translations.literal: Youde led his army back to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Youde marched back to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 定國使張勝、郭有銘為前鋒，趨嚴關，而令雙禮與高文貴、靳統武繼其後。

translations.literal: Dingguo sent Zhang Sheng and Guo Youming as vanguard to hurry to Yanguan, and ordered Feng Shuangli with Gao Wengui and Jin Tongwu to follow after.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo sent Zhang Sheng and Guo Youming ahead toward Yanguan and Feng Shuangli, Gao Wengui, and Jin Tongwu after.

sentences.zh: 有德遣兵逆戰驛湖，敗績，陷全州。

translations.literal: Youde sent troops to meet them in battle at Yihu; they were defeated; Quanzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Youde sent troops to Yihu and was beaten; Quanzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 定國與王之邦、劉之講、吳子聖、廖魚、卜寧率所部自西延大埠疾馳嚮桂林，勝、有銘已破嚴關。

translations.literal: Dingguo with Wang Zhibang, Liu Zhijiang, Wu Zisheng, Liao Yu, and Bu Ning led their troops at a gallop from Xiyan Dabu toward Guilin; Sheng and Youming had already broken Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo raced from Xiyan Dabu toward Guilin with Wang Zhibang, Liu Zhijiang, Wu Zisheng, Liao Yu, and Bu Ning; Sheng and Youming had already forced Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 有德率師出戰，定國軍中象陣略退，斬馭象者以徇，所部戰甚力，驅象突陣，有德敗績，退保桂林。

translations.literal: Youde led his army out to fight; the elephant corps in Dingguo's army fell back slightly; Dingguo beheaded the mahouts to warn the ranks; his troops fought fiercely; he drove the elephants to break the formation; Youde was defeated and withdrew to hold Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Youde marched out to fight; Dingguo's elephant line wavered; he beheaded the mahouts as an example; his men fought furiously and drove the elephants through the enemy line; Youde was beaten back to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 定國晝夜環攻，城陷，有德自殺。

translations.literal: Dingguo besieged day and night; the city fell; Youde killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo besieged the city without rest; it fell; Youde took his own life.

sentences.zh: 定國分兵徇廣西諸郡縣，梧州、柳州皆下，又遣白文選攻陷辰州。

translations.literal: Dingguo divided his troops to sweep the prefectures and counties of Guangxi; Wuzhou and Liuzhou both fell; he also sent Bai Wenxuan to attack and take Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo sent columns through Guangxi; Wuzhou and Liuzhou fell; he sent Bai Wenxuan to take Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 大將軍敬謹親王尼堪率師南征，次湘潭。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince Jing of Jingjin Niken led the imperial army south in campaign and halted at Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Prince Jingjin Niken marched south and stopped at Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 馬進忠引退，師從之，次衡州。

translations.literal: Ma Jinzhong withdrew; the imperial army followed and halted at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jinzhong fell back; the Qing army followed to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 定國赴援，兩軍同時至，戰衡州城下，定國敗走。

translations.literal: Dingguo hastened to the relief; both armies arrived at the same time; they fought below the walls of Hengzhou; Dingguo was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo hurried to help; both armies reached Hengzhou together; they fought below the walls; Dingguo was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 敬謹親王自率精騎追之，遇伏，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Prince Jingjin personally led elite cavalry in pursuit; he encountered an ambush and perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingjin himself led crack horsemen in pursuit, ran into an ambush, and was killed in the fight.

sentences.zh: 定國收兵屯武岡。

translations.literal: Dingguo gathered his troops and encamped at Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo pulled his forces together and held Wugang.

sentences.zh: 定國轉戰廣西、湖廣，下數十城，兵屢勝，可望益嫉之，次沅州，召定國計事，將以衡州敗為定國罪而殺之。

translations.literal: Dingguo campaigned through Guangxi and Huguang, took dozens of cities, and his army won repeatedly; Kewang grew ever more jealous; encamped at Yuanzhou, he summoned Dingguo to consult on affairs, intending to make Dingguo's crime the defeat at Hengzhou and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo fought across Guangxi and Huguang, capturing dozens of towns in a run of victories. Kewang's jealousy sharpened. At Yuanzhou he summoned Dingguo under pretense of consultation, planning to charge him with the Hengzhou defeat and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 定國察其意，辭不赴。

translations.literal: Dingguo discerned his intent and declined to go, pleading an excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo saw through the scheme and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 十年，率進忠等犯永州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he led Jin Zhong and others to attack Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he marched on Yongzhou with Jin Zhong and others.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、貝勒屯齊率師自衡州赴之，未至，定國度龍虎關復入廣西，次柳州。

translations.literal: The Great General, Prince Tunqi, led the army from Hengzhou to meet him; before he arrived, Dingguo crossed Longhu Pass back into Guangxi and encamped at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Great General Prince Tunqi marched from Hengzhou to intercept him, but before he arrived Dingguo had crossed Longhu Pass back into Guangxi and halted at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 可望會雙禮追定國，自靖州進次寶慶。

translations.literal: Kewang joined with Shuangli in pursuing Dingguo, advancing from Jingzhou to encamp at Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang and Shuangli gave chase from Jingzhou and pitched camp at Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 貝勒屯齊遣兵自永州要擊，可望敗走，還貴陽。

translations.literal: Prince Tunqi sent troops from Yongzhou to intercept them; Kewang was defeated and fled, returning to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tunqi sent a force from Yongzhou to cut them off; Kewang was beaten and fled back to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 定國自柳州道懷集，攻肇慶。

translations.literal: Dingguo went from Liuzhou by way of Huaiji to attack Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: From Liuzhou Dingguo passed through Huaiji and struck at Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 師自廣州赴援，戰四會河口，定國兵敗，移軍破長樂，行略高、雷、廉三府，悉屬於定國。

translations.literal: The imperial army marched from Guangzhou to the relief; they fought at the mouth of the Si River; Dingguo's army was defeated; he shifted his force, took Changle, then overran the three prefectures of Gao, Lei, and Lian, all of which came under Dingguo's control.
translations.idiomatic: Qing forces marched from Guangzhou to relieve the city and fought at the Si River estuary. Dingguo was defeated, but he wheeled away, took Changle, and swept through the prefectures of Gao, Lei, and Lian until all three lay in his hands.

sentences.zh: 桂王在安隆，馬吉翔為政，遙奉可望指。

translations.literal: The Gui Prince was at Anlong; Ma Jixiang handled government affairs and from afar obeyed Kewang's directions.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongli Emperor held court at Anlong while Ma Jixiang ran affairs, taking his cues from Kewang at a distance.

sentences.zh: 可望謀自帝甚急，王懼，與大學士吳貞毓謀密遣林青陽敕定國統兵入衛，定國感泣，議奉迎，青陽密使報王。

translations.literal: Kewang's plot to make himself emperor grew urgent; the prince was afraid; with Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu he secretly sent Lin Qingyang with an edict ordering Dingguo to command troops to enter and guard the throne; Dingguo wept in emotion and agreed to come and welcome the prince; Qingyang secretly sent word to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang's bid for the throne turned frantic. The emperor in alarm plotted with Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu to send Lin Qingyang secretly with orders for Dingguo to march in and protect the court. Dingguo wept and pledged to escort the sovereign north. Qingyang sent secret word back to the court.

sentences.zh: 王復遣周官鑄屏翰親臣金印賜之，定國拜受命。

translations.literal: The prince again sent Zhou Guan to cast a golden seal inscribed "Pillar and Screen, Close Minister" and bestow it on him; Dingguo bowed and accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Zhou Guan to cast and bestow a golden seal naming Dingguo a pillar of the throne; Dingguo bowed and accepted the charge.

sentences.zh: 十一年，事為吉翔聞，啟可望，可望怒，遣其將鄭國按治，殺貞毓、青陽及諸與謀者凡十八人，獨官走免。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the matter came to Jixiang's ears; he reported it to Kewang; Kewang was enraged and sent his general Zheng Guo to investigate and punish them; he killed Zhenyu, Qingyang, and all the conspirators, eighteen persons in all; only Guan escaped by flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Jixiang heard of the plot and informed Kewang. Enraged, Kewang sent his general Zheng Guo to root it out. Zhenyu, Qingyang, and every co-conspirator—eighteen in all—were killed; only Zhou Guan fled and survived.

sentences.zh: 定國發兵陷高明，進圍新城。

translations.literal: Dingguo raised troops, took Gaoming, and advanced to besiege Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo marched out, captured Gaoming, and pushed on to besiege Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 平南王尚可喜、靖南王耿繼茂赴援，次三水，將軍珠瑪喇以師會，戰於珊洲，定國兵敗，退保新會。

translations.literal: Prince Pingnan Shang Kexi and Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao hurried to the relief; they encamped at Sanshui; General Zhumaraha joined them with the army; they fought at Shanzhou; Dingguo's army was defeated and fell back to hold Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Shang Kexi and Geng Jimao hurried to relieve the city, halting at Sanshui. General Zhumaraha brought up the Qing army to join them. At Shanzhou Dingguo was beaten and withdrew to defend Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 師進擊之，定國敗走。

translations.literal: The imperial army pressed the attack; Dingguo was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army pressed on; Dingguo broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 十二年，師進次興業，再進次橫州江上。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the army advanced and encamped at Xingye, then advanced again to encamp on the river at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Qing army halted at Xingye, then moved on again to the river line at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 定國戰屢敗，乃道賓州走南寧。

translations.literal: Dingguo was repeatedly defeated in battle; then he went by way of Binzhou and fled to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: After a string of defeats Dingguo retreated through Binzhou to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 可喜等撫定高、雷、廉三府及廣西橫州。

translations.literal: Kexi and the others pacified the three prefectures of Gao, Lei, and Lian and Hengzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi and his allies settled the prefectures of Gao, Lei, and Lian and brought Hengzhou in Guangxi back under control.

sentences.zh: 十三年，師進攻南寧，定國戰復敗，將道安隆入雲南。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the army advanced to attack Nanning; Dingguo was again defeated in battle; he was about to go by way of Anlong into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Qing army pushed on Nanning. Dingguo lost again and prepared to withdraw through Anlong into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 可望詗知之，遣白文選移桂王貴陽。

translations.literal: Kewang learned of it through espionage and sent Bai Wenxuan to move the Gui Prince to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang learned of the move through spies and ordered Bai Wenxuan to transfer the emperor to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 文選心不直可望，因密告王曰：「姑遲行，候西府。」

translations.literal: Wenxuan's heart was not loyal to Kewang; he therefore secretly told the prince, "For the moment delay your departure and wait for the Western Headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan had no loyalty to Kewang. He secretly told the emperor, "Do not move yet—wait for the Western Headquarters."

sentences.zh: 西府謂定國也。

translations.literal: The Western Headquarters" meant Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Headquarters meant Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 定國至，文選與共奉王自安南入雲南。

translations.literal: When Dingguo arrived, Wenxuan joined him in escorting the prince from Annan into Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingguo arrived, Wenxuan joined him in escorting the emperor from Annan into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 文秀自四川還軍，可望令與諸將王尚禮、王自奇守雲南，亦不直可望，遂與沐天波迓王入居可望廨，進定國晉王，並封文秀、文選皆王，尚禮等公。

translations.literal: Wenxiu returned with his army from Sichuan; Kewang ordered him with the generals Wang Shangli and Wang Ziqi to guard Yunnan; he too was not loyal to Kewang; therefore with Mu Tianbo he welcomed the prince to take up residence in Kewang's headquarters; Dingguo was advanced to Prince of Jin; Wenxiu and Wenxuan were both enfeoffed as princes; Shangli and the others as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu came back from Sichuan with his troops. Kewang had ordered him, Wang Shangli, and Wang Ziqi to hold Yunnan, but Wenxiu too had turned against him. With Mu Tianbo he welcomed the emperor into Kewang's old headquarters, raised Dingguo to Prince of Jin, enfeoffed Wenxiu and Wenxuan as princes, and Shangli and the rest as dukes.

sentences.zh: 令文選還貴陽喻意，可望奪文選兵，置之軍中。

translations.literal: Dingguo ordered Wenxuan to return to Guiyang to convey his meaning; Kewang stripped Wenxuan of his troops and placed him in the army camp under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was sent back to Guiyang to carry Dingguo's terms. Kewang seized his troops and kept him under guard in camp.

sentences.zh: 定國令靳統武收吉翔，將殺之，吉翔哀統武為言于定國，召入謁，叩頭，諂定國，定國薦於王，使入閣，復用事。

translations.literal: Dingguo ordered Jin Tongwu to seize Jixiang and was about to kill him; Jixiang begged Tongwu to speak for him to Dingguo; he was summoned to audience, kowtowed, and flattered Dingguo; Dingguo recommended him to the prince, had him enter the Secretariat, and he again wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo ordered Jin Tongwu to arrest Jixiang and was set to execute him. Jixiang begged Tongwu to intercede, was brought in, kowtowed, and poured on flattery until Dingguo recommended him to the emperor. Jixiang reentered the Secretariat and again held power.

sentences.zh: 十四年，可望舉兵反攻定國，起文選為將，留雙禮守貴陽。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Kewang raised troops to counterattack Dingguo; he restored Wenxuan as general and left Shuangli to guard Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Kewang turned his army on Dingguo, put Wenxuan back in command, and left Shuangli to hold Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 定國與文秀率師禦之，遇於三岔河。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Wenxiu led the army to resist him; they met at Sanhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Wenxiu marched out to meet him at Sanhe River.

sentences.zh: 兩軍夾河而陣，文選棄其軍奔定國，可望遣張勝、馬寶自尋甸間道襲雲南，而自將當定國，戰方合，其將馬維興先奔，兵盡潰，可望走還貴陽。

translations.literal: The two armies drew up facing each other across the river; Wenxuan abandoned his army and fled to Dingguo; Kewang sent Zhang Sheng and Ma Bao by a secret route from Xundian to strike Yunnan, while he himself took command against Dingguo; as the battle was just joined, his general Ma Weixing was the first to flee; the army completely collapsed; Kewang fled back to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies faced off across the river. Wenxuan deserted his command and ran to Dingguo. Kewang sent Zhang Sheng and Ma Bao by a back road from Xundian to raid Yunnan while he himself blocked Dingguo. The fight had barely begun when Ma Weixing broke first; the whole army unraveled and Kewang fled back to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 定國遣文秀追可望，引軍還雲南，遇勝於渾水塘，獲而殺之，寶降定國。

translations.literal: Dingguo sent Wenxiu to pursue Kewang, led the army back to Yunnan, met Sheng at Hunshuitang, captured and killed him; Bao surrendered to Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo sent Wenxiu after Kewang and marched back toward Yunnan. At Hunshuitang they caught Zhang Sheng and killed him; Ma Bao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 可望至貴陽，雙禮言追兵且至，可望乃詣經略洪承疇降。

translations.literal: When Kewang reached Guiyang, Shuangli said pursuing troops were about to arrive; Kewang then went to Regional Commander Hong Chengchou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang reached Guiyang. Shuangli warned that pursuers were close, and Kewang went to Regional Commander Hong Chengchou and submitted.

sentences.zh: 雙禮盡取其子女玉帛，從文秀歸雲南，桂王進雙禮王、維興等公。

translations.literal: Shuangli took all his sons, daughters, jade, and silks; he followed Wenxiu back to Yunnan; the Gui Prince advanced Shuangli to prince and Weixing and the others to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangli stripped him of his family, jewels, and goods and returned to Yunnan with Wenxiu. The emperor raised Shuangli to princely rank and Weixing and the others to dukes.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大將軍羅讬自湖南，吳三桂自四川，將軍卓布泰自廣西，三道入貴州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Great General Luotuo from Hunan, Wu Sangui from Sichuan, and General Zhuobutai from Guangxi entered Guizhou by three routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year three Qing columns marched into Guizhou: Great General Luotuo from Hunan, Wu Sangui from Sichuan, and General Zhuobutai from Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 文秀病卒。

translations.literal: Wenxiu died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu died of illness.

sentences.zh: 定國使劉正國、楊武守三坡、紅關諸隘，禦三桂，馬進忠守貴州。

translations.literal: Dingguo sent Liu Zhengguo and Yang Wu to hold the passes at Sanpo, Hongguan, and other defiles to resist Wu Sangui; Ma Jinzhong guarded Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo posted Liu Zhengguo and Yang Wu at Sanpo, Hongguan, and the other passes to block Wu Sangui, and left Ma Jinzhong to hold Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 會王自奇、關有才貳于定國，據永昌舉兵，定國自將擊之。

translations.literal: Just then Wang Ziqi and Guan Youcai rebelled against Dingguo, seized Yongchang, and raised troops; Dingguo personally led the attack against them.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Wang Ziqi and Guan Youcai turned against Dingguo, seized Yongchang, and rebelled. Dingguo marched against them in person.

sentences.zh: 羅讬師自鎮遠入，定國不及援，卓布泰亦盡下南丹、那地、獨山諸州，兩軍會貴陽，進忠遁去。

translations.literal: Luotuo's army entered from Zhenyuan; Dingguo could not arrive in time to relieve them; Zhuobutai also took all the prefectures of Nandan, Nadi, and Dushan; the two armies joined at Guiyang; Jinzhong fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Luotuo's column entered from Zhenyuan before Dingguo could help. Zhuobutai overran Nandan, Nadi, Dushan, and the rest. The two Qing armies met at Guiyang and Jinzhong fled.

sentences.zh: 三桂師後入，至三坡，正國拒戰，大敗，自水西奔還雲南。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's army entered afterward, reached Sanpo; Zhengguo resisted in battle and was utterly defeated; he fled back to Yunnan by way of Shuixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui came up later to Sanpo. Zhengguo resisted and was crushed, fleeing back to Yunnan through Shuixi.

sentences.zh: 師次開州，武迎戰倒流水，亦敗，遂取遵義。

translations.literal: The army encamped at Kaizhou; Wu met them in battle at Daoliushui and was also defeated; they then took Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army halted at Kaizhou. Yang Wu fought them at Daoliushui and was beaten too, and Zunyi fell.

sentences.zh: 王拜定國招討大元帥，賜黃鉞，?謀禦敵。

translations.literal: The prince enfeoffed Dingguo as Grand Marshal for Punitive Campaigns, granted him the yellow battle-axe, and entrusted him to plan the defense against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Dingguo Grand Marshal for Punitive Campaigns, gave him the yellow battle-axe of command, and charged him to plan the defense.

sentences.zh: 三桂亦入貴陽，大將軍信郡王多尼至軍，會師平越，戒期入雲南。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui also entered Guiyang; Great General Prince Xinjun Duoni arrived at the army; the forces joined at Pingyue and set a day to enter Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui entered Guiyang as well. Great General Prince Xinjun Duoni joined the campaign; the armies united at Pingyue and fixed a date to invade Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 定國與雙禮扼公背，圖復貴州，文選守七星關。

translations.literal: Dingguo and Shuangli held Chicken Rooster Ridge, intending to recover Guizhou; Wenxuan guarded Qixing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and Shuangli blocked Chicken Rooster Ridge, hoping to retake Guizhou, while Wenxuan held Qixing Pass.

sentences.zh: 三桂師自遵義趨天生橋，出水西，克烏撒，文選棄關走霑益。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's army hurried from Zunyi toward Tiansheng Bridge, issued from Shuixi, took Wusa; Wenxuan abandoned the pass and fled to Zhanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui raced from Zunyi toward Tiansheng Bridge, broke out through Shuixi, and took Wusa. Wenxuan abandoned the pass and fled to Zhanyi.

sentences.zh: 卓布泰兵次盤江，自下流宵濟，遂入安隆，定國將吳子聖拒戰，敗走。

translations.literal: Zhuobutai's troops encamped at the Pan River; at night they crossed from downstream; they then entered Anlong; Dingguo's general Wu Zisheng resisted in battle and was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuobutai halted at the Pan River and crossed by night from downstream, then pushed into Anlong. Wu Zisheng tried to stop him, was beaten, and fled.

sentences.zh: 定國以全軍據雙河口，卓布泰師進破象陣，迭戰羅炎、涼水井，定國兵潰，妻子俱散失，諸將竄走不相顧。

translations.literal: Dingguo with his entire army held Shuanghekou; Zhuobutai's army advanced, broke the elephant formation, and fought in succession at Luoyan and Liangshuijing; Dingguo's army collapsed; his wife and children were all scattered and lost; the generals fled in all directions without looking back for one another.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo massed his whole force at Shuanghekou. Zhuobutai broke his elephant line and fought through Luoyan and Liangshuijing in succession. Dingguo's army fell apart; his wife and children were lost in the rout, and his generals fled without a thought for one another.

sentences.zh: 定國收兵還雲南，奉桂王走永昌。

translations.literal: Dingguo gathered his troops, returned to Yunnan, and escorted the Gui Prince in flight to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo regrouped, withdrew to Yunnan, and escorted the emperor in flight to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，師自普安入雲南會城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year the army entered the Yunnan capital from Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year the Qing army entered the Yunnan capital from Pu'an.

sentences.zh: 定國使靳統武護桂王走騰越，文選自霑益追及定國，定國使斷後，屯玉龍關。

translations.literal: Dingguo sent Jin Tongwu to escort the Gui Prince in flight to Tengyue; Wenxuan from Zhanyi caught up with Dingguo; Dingguo had him cover the retreat and encamped at Yulong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo sent Jin Tongwu to escort the emperor toward Tengyue. Wenxuan caught up from Zhanyi and was left to cover the retreat at Yulong Pass.

sentences.zh: 師從之，文選戰而敗，自右甸走木邦，師遂克永昌，渡潞江，陟磨盤山。

translations.literal: The imperial army pursued; Wenxuan fought and was defeated; he fled from Youdian to Mohang; the army then took Yongchang, crossed the Lu River, and climbed Moganshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army pursued. Wenxuan fought, lost, and withdrew from Youdian into Mohang. The invaders took Yongchang, crossed the Lu River, and climbed Moganshan.

sentences.zh: 定國使其將竇民望、高文貴、王璽為三伏以待。

translations.literal: Dingguo had his generals Dou Minwang, Gao Wengui, and Wang Xi set three ambushes to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo posted three ambushes under Dou Minwang, Gao Wengui, and Wang Xi.

sentences.zh: 師半度，以?發其伏，伏起力戰，自卯至午短兵接，死者如堵牆。

translations.literal: When the army was half across, cannon fire sprung the ambush; the ambushers rose and fought with all their strength; from the hour mao to the hour wu they closed at close quarters; the dead piled like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing column was half across, cannon fire sprung the trap. The hidden troops surged up and fought hand to hand from dawn till midday; the dead heaped up like a rampart.

sentences.zh: 民望彈穿脅，猶持刀潰圍出，乃死。

translations.literal: Minwang was shot through the flank; still clutching his blade he broke out of the encirclement before he died.
translations.idiomatic: A bullet tore through Minwang's side, yet he cut his way out of the ring with a blade in hand before he fell.

sentences.zh: 璽亦死於陣。

translations.literal: Xi also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xi too was killed in the fight.

sentences.zh: 定國坐山巔督戰，飛?墮其前，土坌起撲面，遂奔，退走騰越。

translations.literal: Dingguo sat on the mountain peak directing the battle; a cannonball fell before him; dust rose up and struck his face; he then fled and withdrew toward Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo directed the fight from the ridge until a cannonball struck near him, dust flying into his face. He broke and withdrew toward Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 未至，馬吉翔以桂王走南甸。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Ma Jixiang had already taken the Gui Prince in flight to Nandian.
translations.idiomatic: Before he got there, Ma Jixiang had already fled with the emperor to Nandian.

sentences.zh: 統武還從定國，雙禮渡金沙江走建昌，其部將執以出降。

translations.literal: Tongwu returned to follow Dingguo; Shuangli crossed the Jinsha River and fled toward Jianchang; his subordinate officers seized him and surrendered him to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Tongwu rejoined Dingguo. Shuangli fled across the Jinsha toward Jianchang, but his own officers seized him and surrendered him.

sentences.zh: 王，與定國意?桂王入緬甸，定國次孟艮，如木邦，從文選謀，分屯邊境。

translations.literal: The prince and Dingguo agreed that the Gui Prince should enter Burma; Dingguo encamped at Menggen, went to Mohang, and following Wenxuan's plan divided forces along the border.
translations.idiomatic: The court and Dingguo agreed to send the emperor into Burma. Dingguo halted at Menggen, moved on Mohang, and by Wenxuan's counsel scattered pickets along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 文選將入異。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was about to enter Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan prepared to cross into Burma.

sentences.zh: 定國乃移駐猛緬，收殘部，勢稍振。

translations.literal: Dingguo then shifted his headquarters to Mengmian, gathered the remnant forces, and his strength was somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo then moved to Mengmian, rallied the remnants, and his force began to recover.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復移駐孟連。

translations.literal: Before long he moved his headquarters again to Menglian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he shifted again to Menglian.

sentences.zh: 賀九儀招文秀將張國用、趙得勝歸定國。

translations.literal: He Jiuyi recruited Wenxiu's generals Zhang Guoyong and Zhao Desheng to return to Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He Jiuyi drew Wenxiu's generals Zhang Guoyong and Zhao Desheng back to Dingguo's side.

sentences.zh: 孟艮酋懼定國兼?，攻定國，定國擊破之，遂據其地。

translations.literal: The chief of Menggen feared Dingguo would annex his territory; he attacked Dingguo; Dingguo defeated and broke him, then seized the region.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of Menggen, fearing annexation, attacked Dingguo and was crushed. Dingguo then held the territory himself.

sentences.zh: 號召諸土司起兵，元江土司那嵩應定國，三桂討焉，嵩自焚死。

translations.literal: He called upon the native chiefs to raise troops; the Yuanjiang chief Nasong answered Dingguo; Wu Sangui campaigned against him; Nasong burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: He called the native chiefs to arms. Nasong of Yuanjiang answered him, but Wu Sangui marched against him and Nasong burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 三桂使招九儀，定國執而殺之。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui sent envoys to win over Jiuyi; Dingguo seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui tried to win Jiuyi over; Dingguo arrested and executed him.

sentences.zh: 國用、得勝皆鞅鞅不為用，定國坐是終不競。

translations.literal: Guoyong and Desheng were both discontented and unwilling to serve wholeheartedly; because of this Dingguo in the end could not contend successfully.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyong and Desheng sulked and would not commit fully, and for that reason Dingguo never regained real strength.

sentences.zh: 十七年，文選自木邦攻阿瓦，求出桂王，不克，引兵會定國孟艮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Wenxuan from Mohang attacked Ava, seeking to bring out the Gui Prince; he did not succeed; he led his troops to join Dingguo at Menggen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Wenxuan marched from Mohang against Ava to recover the emperor, failed, and withdrew to join Dingguo at Menggen.

sentences.zh: 十八年，合兵復攻阿瓦，定國上三十餘疏迎桂王，為吉翔所阻，不得達。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year they combined forces to attack Ava again; Dingguo submitted more than thirty memorials welcoming the Gui Prince; Jixiang blocked them and they did not reach the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year they attacked Ava again together. Dingguo sent more than thirty memorials pleading to bring the emperor out, but Jixiang blocked every one.

sentences.zh: 文選使密啟王，得報書。

translations.literal: Wenxuan sent a secret message to the prince and received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan got a secret message through to the emperor and received an answer.

sentences.zh: 與緬人戰，定國軍稍?，文選引兵橫擊之，緬人大敗，退城守，然終不肯出桂王。

translations.literal: In fighting the Burmese, Dingguo's army suffered a slight setback; Wenxuan led troops in a flanking strike; the Burmese were utterly defeated and withdrew to hold the city, yet in the end they still refused to release the Gui Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting with the Burmese Dingguo's line wavered until Wenxuan swung his troops across and smashed them. The Burmese fled behind their walls, but still would not surrender the emperor.

sentences.zh: 復議以舟師攻之，造船，為緬人所焚，乃移兵次洞鄔，國用、得勝挾文選北走，定國還孟艮。

translations.literal: They again discussed attacking by river fleet; they built boats, but the Burmese burned them; they then shifted their troops to encamp at Dongwu; Guoyong and Desheng forced Wenxuan away north; Dingguo returned to Menggen.
translations.idiomatic: They planned a river assault, built boats, and watched the Burmese burn them. The army moved to Dongwu; Guoyong and Desheng then seized Wenxuan and fled north, while Dingguo withdrew to Menggen.

sentences.zh: 文選至耿馬，遇定國將吳三省，方得定國妻子，將歸諸定國，乃合軍駐錫箔，憑江為險。

translations.literal: Wenxuan reached Gengma and met Dingguo's general Wu Sansheng, who had just recovered Dingguo's wife and children and was about to return them to Dingguo; they then combined their armies and encamped at Xibo, relying on the river as a defense.
translations.idiomatic: At Gengma Wenxuan met Wu Sansheng, who had recovered Dingguo's wife and children and was bringing them back. They united at Xibo and made the river their rampart.

sentences.zh: 三桂與將軍愛星阿會木邦，倍道深入，文選降。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui and General Ai Xing'a joined forces at Mohang, marched by forced stages deep into the interior, and Wenxuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and General Ai Xing'a united at Mohang, pushed deep by forced marches, and Wenxuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 師薄阿瓦，緬人執王歸於我師。

translations.literal: The army pressed close to Ava; the Burmese seized the prince and delivered him to our army.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army closed on Ava; the Burmese handed the emperor over to them.

sentences.zh: 定國自景線走猛臘，遣將入車裏、暹羅諸國乞師，皆不應；

translations.literal: Dingguo fled from Jingxian to Mengla and sent generals into Cheli, Siam, and other states to beg for troops; none answered;
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo withdrew from Jingxian to Mengla and sent envoys to Cheli, Siam, and other kingdoms begging for aid; none would help;

sentences.zh: 伺邊上求王消息。

translations.literal: he kept watch along the frontier seeking news of the prince.
translations.idiomatic: he kept watch along the border for word of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，聞王凶問，號慟祈死。
