translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he heard mournful news of the prince's death; he wailed in grief and prayed for death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he learned that the emperor was dead; he wailed in grief and prayed to die.

sentences.zh: 六月壬子，其生日也，病作，誡其子及靳統武曰：「任死荒徼，毋降！」

translations.literal: On renzi, the sixth month, which was his birthday, illness came upon him; he admonished his son and Jin Tongwu, saying, "Better to die on this remote frontier than surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day in the sixth month—his birthday—he fell ill and told his son and Jin Tongwu, "Better to die on this wild frontier than submit!"

sentences.zh: 乙丑，定國卒。

translations.literal: On yichou, Dingguo died.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Dingguo died.

sentences.zh: 統武尋亦卒。

translations.literal: Tongwu soon died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Tongwu died soon after.

sentences.zh: 嗣興乃與文秀子震率所部出降。

translations.literal: Sixing then together with Wenxiu's son Zhen led their respective commands out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sixing and Wenxiu's son Zhen then led their remaining troops out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當鼎革之際，勝國遣臣舉兵圖興復，時勢既去，不可為而為，蓋鮮有濟者。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the time of the dynastic transformation, loyal ministers of the fallen dynasty raised armies seeking restoration; the tide of fortune had already turned; to do what could not be done—there were scarcely any who succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In the chaos of dynastic change, loyalists of the fallen Ming took up arms to restore the throne. Fortune had already turned; few who pressed on against that tide ever prevailed.

sentences.zh: 徒以忠義鬱結，深入于人心，陵谷可得更，精誠不可得沫。

translations.literal: Yet because loyalty and righteousness were deeply knotted and had sunk into people's hearts, hills and valleys may be changed but sincere devotion cannot be erased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyalty and righteousness had sunk deep into the people's hearts. Mountains and valleys may shift, but such devotion cannot be washed away.

sentences.zh: 煌言勢窮兵散，終不肯為逭死之計。

translations.literal: Huangyan, though his strength was exhausted and his soldiers scattered, to the end refused any plan of escape from death.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyan, though ruined and alone, would not even contemplate saving his own life.

sentences.zh: 成功大舉不克，退求自保，存先代正朔。

translations.literal: Chenggong, when his great campaign failed, withdrew to seek self-preservation and preserved the former dynasty's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong, after his great expedition failed, withdrew to hold on and keep the old calendar alive.

sentences.zh: 定國以降將受命敗軍後，崎嶇險阻，百折而不撓，比之擴廓帖木兒、陳友定輩，何多讓焉。

translations.literal: Dingguo, a surrendered general who received his commission after defeat, through rugged hardship and a hundred setbacks never bent; compared with Kulai Temür, Chen Youding, and such men, how much reason would he have to yield place?
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo was a turncoat general who took command after defeat, yet he endured a hundred setbacks on brutal roads without bending. Compared with Kulai Temür or Chen Youding, he has little to yield.

sentences.zh: 即用明史例，次於開國?雄之列。

translations.literal: Following the precedent of the History of Ming, he is placed next among the heroes of the founding age.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Ming History's precedent, he is ranked among the founding heroes.

sentences.zh: 既表先代遺忠，並以見其倔強山海間，遠至三十餘年，近亦十餘年。

translations.literal: This both sets forth the loyal devotion of the former dynasty and shows how stubbornly they held out among mountains and seas—some for more than thirty years, others for more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: The record honors the old dynasty's loyalists and shows how stubbornly they held out in the hills and along the coast—some for more than thirty years, others for a decade or more.

sentences.zh: 開創艱難，卒能定於一，非偶然也。

translations.literal: That the founding of the dynasty was arduous yet in the end was settled in unity was no accident.
translations.idiomatic: That the Qing founding was hard won yet ended in unity was no accident.
